title: Medium objects never reuse swept blocks: heap grows with medium allocation volume, past --heap-limit-mib
description:
HeapState::replace_overflow (src/eval/memory/heap.rs, ~line 595) always takes BumpBlock::new(); it never reuses a swept or recycled block. Medium objects (> one line, < one block: set/vec storage of ~1000 elements) therefore always land in fresh blocks. Swept blocks are consumed only by head replacement, so a workload dominated by medium allocations grows the heap by its medium allocation volume no matter how little is live.

Repro (release, EU_PP_THRESHOLD=999999999):
  n: 32000
  base: range(0, 1000) set.from-list
  step(s, i): s set.remove(i % 1000) set.add(i % 1000)
  r: foldl(step, base, range(0, n)) set.size
Peak heap blocks scale with n: 3,757 / 7,842 / 17,066 / 34,345 for n = 4k/8k/16k/32k (deterministic), Blocks Recycled 0. Under --heap-limit-mib 256 the n=32000 run ends at 34,638 blocks (~1.08 GB, 4x the cap) and succeeds: measured live after each collection is 8..2,051 blocks, so the live-based limit check never fires. Under the 32 GiB default such a program grows until the kernel kills it.

Diagnostic (throwaway, not a fix): letting replace_overflow take a fully free recycled block (lazily sweeping unswept) cut the n=32000 peak to 11,779 blocks unbounded / 9,765 at a 256 MiB cap. The remainder is live data held by a 128,010-deep stack: the foldl accumulator here is not strict (Max Stack 4n), which may be a separate eu-oaz72.27/.34 gap.

Measured on master 1d1de2e; see docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-eu-oaz72.4-acceptance.md.

Originally filed by the eu-oaz72.4 lane (PR #1166) under the id eu-oaz72.55 by mistake: that id belongs to the closed large-object bead, which this relay overwrote. Re-filed here by the coordinator.
design:
1. Free-block pool: sweeping sorts reclaimable blocks into 'free' (no marked line) and 'recycled' (holes). replace_overflow(size) takes a free block (lazily sweeping unswept until one appears), else a recycled block whose largest hole fits (bounded scan), else a fresh block. Head replacement takes recycled, then free, then fresh. Medium objects then reuse swept space and the heap stops growing with medium allocation volume.
2. Footprint limit: under --heap-limit-mib, the GC policy also fires once blocks held (bump blocks plus large-object blocks) exceed the limit. After a collection under a limit, finish the deferred sweep and release free blocks to the system until held <= 7/8 of the limit; if held still exceeds the limit, raise HeapLimitExceeded (held MiB vs limit). So blocks held, not only measured live, respect the limit (overshoot bounded by one poll interval).
3. Tests: unit tests for overflow reuse and footprint trimming; harness/bench-style regression on the set-churn repro checking peak independent of n, fault-injection verified.
acceptance_criteria: Medium-object churn (the set repro above, n=32000) runs with a peak heap independent of n, within the cap under --heap-limit-mib 256 or with a heap-limit error; footprint (blocks held), not only measured live, respects the limit; regression test fault-injection verified; two independent rig-reviews (GC area).
notes: Merged in PR #1171 (two independent rig-reviews per round, two rounds). Criterion 1 is judged on the forced-accumulator form: peak 1,030 blocks at n = 4k/16k/64k. The original foldl repro still grows with n unbounded because its accumulator is non-strict (Max Stack 4n+10, live data), which is eu-oaz72.27's territory. Under --heap-limit-mib 256, n=32k peaks at about 7,728-7,873 blocks against the 8,192 cap (master: 34,638). The footprint is enforced: trigger at 7/8 of the limit, free blocks released down to 3/4, and HeapLimitExceeded after two successive collections hold more than the limit plus half of it (at least 1 MiB) as fragmentation tolerance. Report: docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-eu-oaz72.73-medium-block-reuse.md.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1171

title: (BUG) GC never frees large-object blocks (HeapState::lobs only grows) and never prunes line_map_index
description: Reported by the eu-oaz72.4 lane (PR #1142): large-object blocks (>32 KB) are never freed (HeapState::lobs only grows), so large-object churn leaks without bound; the new line_map_index is never pruned. GC/memory defects are P0 (plan §2). eu-y6fx's large-object mark diagnostic now fires in normal runs: investigate together. Fix: sweep unmarked large objects and return their blocks; prune dead line-map entries. Gating test under a small --heap-limit-mib, fault-injection verified; EU_GC_VERIFY=2/POISON/STRESS; two independent rig-reviews. Related from eu-oaz72.51 (PR #1152): perform_emergency_sweep recycles rest blocks against stale line maps, possibly a real hole: check it here or file separately.

Large-object blocks held at exit on the churn test: 3,002 -> 2; peak RSS 260 MB -> 105 MB (measured-single). The emergency-sweep question moved to eu-oaz72.59; reviewer follow-ups in eu-oaz72.61.

title: (BUG?) perform_emergency_sweep recycles rest blocks against stale line maps: suspected GC hole
description: Found by the eu-oaz72.51 lane (PR #1152, merged). perform_emergency_sweep appears to recycle rest blocks using line maps that are stale for the current cycle, so live lines could be handed out as holes. Under EU_GC_POISON, #1152 now poisons every recycled hole and panics with GC HOLE when bump() enters a hole that is no longer all poison, so if this is real it will now show up as a panic under POISON. First step: reproduce under EU_GC_POISON=1 and EU_GC_VERIFY=2 with a small --heap-limit-mib that forces emergency sweeps. If confirmed, raise to P0 (GC bugs are always P0, plan §2) and fix; if refuted, record the evidence and close. Sensitive area: two independent rig-reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Either a reproduction plus a fix with a fault-injection-verified regression test, or a recorded refutation (emergency-sweep path exercised under POISON + VERIFY=2 with no GC HOLE).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1157, merged by the owner at 21:26Z (8e95928). Latent hole confirmed and closed: the emergency sweep now drains only unswept blocks, and strategy 2 is removed. Three unit tests, fault-injection verified. Dead sweep functions are tracked on eu-oaz72.61.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CONFIRMED (latent). perform_emergency_sweep calls HeapState::sweep(), which recycles every rest block against its line map. No mark runs on this path, so a block retired to rest since the last collection (a filled head or overflow) carries a map that predates the objects bumped into it; a fresh block's map is empty, so the whole block is recycled and its live objects reused. Unit test test_emergency_sweep_spares_blocks_retired_since_mark shows it: a live object in a retired head is recycled and overwritten. Reachability: find_space only enters the emergency path when try_allocate fails, and today it cannot fail for any size (small objects fit any recycled hole >= 1 line; medium falls through to a fresh overflow; large gets a LOB; --heap-limit-mib is enforced by the machine via heap_limit_exceeded, not in try_allocate). Every tests/harness/*.eu plus benches 004-022 at --heap-limit-mib 8/16/64 under EU_GC_POISON=1 EU_GC_VERIFY=2: no emergency collection, no GC HOLE, no panic. So no live corruption in released builds, but the code is unsound and one change to try_allocate away from a hole; raised to P0 per instructions as a confirmed GC hole.

DESIGN: emergency sweep must only recycle blocks whose maps describe their contents. Those are exactly the blocks still in unswept (moved there by defer_sweep at the end of the last mark, not allocated into since: the invariant lazy sweep already relies on). Add HeapState::sweep_unswept() (drain lazy_sweep_next) and call it from perform_emergency_sweep instead of sweep(); leave rest alone. Document on HeapState::sweep that it is sound only straight after a mark. Regression test above, fault-injection verified (reverting the call fails both the recycled-list assertion and, separately, the raw-bytes overwrite assertion).

title: GC collects only once the heap limit is reached: OOM kill under the 32 GiB default, thrashing when capped
description:
Heap::policy_requires_collection (src/eval/memory/heap.rs:1767) returns true only when blocks_allocated >= limit, so no collection happens before the limit.
- Default limit is 32 GiB, above the RAM of most machines: `loop(i, a): if(a < 0, a, if(i = 0, a, loop(i - 1, a + 1)))  r: loop(1000000, 0)` with `eu -S` shows Collections 0, 54,727 blocks (~1.7 GB). AoC-sized programs (2025 day04/08/09/10 part 2) are OOM-killed by the kernel within 7-34 s in a 3 GB container, with no eucalypt diagnostic.
- With a limit, the cumulative recycled/allocated ratio (< 0.25) stays true, so it collects on nearly every allocation: same program with --heap-limit-mib 1024 takes 50 s of CollectorMark and 39,326 collections vs 3.7 s unlimited.
Sensitive area (GC): two independent rig-review passes required. Changing the default heap limit is an engine default and is the owner's decision.
acceptance_criteria: Collections trigger on allocation volume since the last GC (not only at the limit); the repro runs with bounded RSS under the default and with --heap-limit-mib 1024 within ~1.5x of unbounded time; a heap-limit exhaustion yields an eucalypt error, not a kernel OOM kill; perf claims follow the performance protocol.
notes:
2026-11-11 owner: GC and memory-management bugs are always top priority (P0) when found.
2026-11-12: (1) a volume-based trigger only pays off once stack retention is fixed (eu-oaz72.34) and accumulators are strict (eu-oaz72.27); measure the 2025 days after those. (2) Small limits thrash even with little live data: the 10x10 day04 test under --heap-limit-mib 16 ran 1,066 collections and 14 s of mark to allocate 32 MB, implying a live floor ~10 MB (prelude etc.); policy should account for the floor. (3) par-* now forks by default (threshold 2), so sequential measurements need EU_PP_THRESHOLD=999999999.
2026-11-12 coordinator: from the eu-oaz72.5 review (PR #1138): the bead's set churn repro (n=16000, release) at --heap-limit-mib 512 peaked at 952 MB RSS (~1.9x the limit) while thrashing for 328 s; unlimited 664 MB in 0.9 s (measured-single). Native storage is now heap-accounted, so include set/vec/ndarray churn in this bead's acceptance measurements, and interpret 'RSS near the limit' explicitly.

Forced set churn: peak 1,030 blocks and RSS 63-64 MB flat for n=4k-32k (before: up to 26,063 blocks / 1,067 MB). Caps 256/64 either complete within the cap or raise HeapLimitExceeded. The loop repro, the 1024 MiB cap (0.98x) and the exhaustion error do not regress. Reports: docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-eu-oaz72.4-acceptance.md (#1166, and the re-run section from #1176) and 2026-11-13-eu-oaz72.73-medium-block-reuse.md (#1171).

title: GC heap values own Rust allocations that are never freed (set, vec, ndarray): move storage into the GC heap
description:
HeapSet::with_added / with_removed / union (src/eval/memory/set.rs:101) clone the whole Rust HashSet, and HeapNdArray::with_set (ndarray.rs:80) clones the array; neither native allocation is freed when the heap object is swept (no Drop/finaliser path).
Repro leak.eu:
  base: range(0, 1000) set.from-list
  step(s, i): s set.remove(i % 1000) set.add(i % 1000)
  r: foldl(step, base, range(0, n)) set.size
With --heap-limit-mib 512: n=4000 -> 482 MB RSS, n=16000 -> 1.79 GB RSS (managed heap capped at 512 MB). Building a set by repeated set.add is O(n^2): 20k elements 7.8 s / 8.7 GB, 30k OOM.
Sensitive area (memory management): two rig-review passes.
acceptance_criteria: No Native variant owns Rust-heap storage (no Rc/Vec/HashMap/String inside heap objects); leak repro (set add/remove churn under --heap-limit-mib 512) keeps RSS bounded near the limit, likewise vec and ndarray churn repros; set/vec/ndarray semantics and to-list order unchanged; passes EU_GC_VERIFY=2, EU_GC_POISON=1, EU_GC_STRESS=1; regression tests fault-injection verified; two independent rig-reviews.
notes:
2026-11-11: no per-object finalisation exists in src/eval/memory (only Block/LargeObjectBlock implement Drop), so every heap object owning a Rust allocation leaks when swept: HeapSet (HashSet), HeapNdArray, and HeapVec (Vec<Primitive>, incl. owned Strings). Also set.from-list is a prelude foldl of set.add (lib/prelude.eu:1973), so building is O(n^2): range(0, 20000) set.from-list takes 10.6 s. A bulk build (one pass) fixes that independently of a persistent representation.
2026-11-11 owner: GC and memory-management bugs are always top priority (P0) when found.
2026-11-11 history: the same no-Drop root cause killed persistent blocks in March 2026 (ADR-001). A finaliser list for every block (PR #387) was judged too costly; here only set/vec/ndarray objects own Rust storage, so a finaliser table restricted to them is a far smaller population - but the alternative is moving their storage into the GC heap (as ROADMAP DS1 proposes for CHAMP). Decide which in the fix design.
2026-11-11 owner decision: fix WITHOUT finalisers. Rule: every heap value's storage lives in the GC heap. Move HeapVec elements into a heap Array (strings as RefPtr<HeapString>, so vec contents are now traced; update the 'GC does not trace into vec' assumption), HeapNdArray f64 data into a heap Array, and HeapSet into a sorted heap Array (copy-on-add stays O(n) for now, but nothing leaks; sets move onto dict nodes later, eu-oaz72.21). Delete the unused Native::Index(Rc<BlockIndex>). Large storage via large-object blocks as usual.
close_reason: Merged in PR #1138 (owner merge after review-round-limit hold): set/vec/ndarray storage now in the GC heap; no Rust-owned allocations or finalisers. Follow-up eu-oaz72.51 (GC HOLE WARNING flood).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design (implementation): (1) set.rs: new Copy element type SetElem {Num(OrderedFloat<f64>), Str(RefPtr<HeapString>), Sym(SymbolId)} with a total order (num < str < sym, strings by content) matching the old Primitive order. HeapSet = {len, RawArray<SetElem>} kept sorted and deduplicated; contains is binary search, add/remove copy into a fresh heap array (O(n), returns the input set unchanged when add finds / remove misses the element), union/intersect/diff are linear merges, from-list sorts+dedups once (O(n log n)). to-list order unchanged (sorted). (2) vec.rs: HeapVec = {len, RawArray<SetElem>} in insertion order; strings shared as RefPtr<HeapString> (no copy). (3) ndarray.rs: HeapNdArray = {len, rank, shape: RawArray<usize>, data: RawArray<f64>}; intrinsics compute on an ndarray ArrayViewD over the heap slice and copy the (transient, Rust-stack-owned) result into the heap. (4) GC: HeapSet/HeapVec/HeapNdArray implement GcScannable: scan marks backing buffers with mark_raw_bytes and pushes them as OpaqueHeapBytes (so they evacuate), and for set/vec marks+pushes each element string; scan_and_update rewrites backing pointers then element string pointers. scan_native/scan_const push the container as a heap object (it was mark-only). (5) Delete Native::Index and BlockIndex. Allocation happens only inside intrinsics (no GC between), so building before returning is safe. Large storage goes through alloc_bytes_uninit -> LOB as for strings.

title: List traversal retains the whole list: range/iterate + count/foldl cost ~10µs per cell and grow superlinearly
description:
Measured on master cb1cc36, release build, with and without lib/prelude.blob (cargo xtask prelude-compile): no difference.

- x: range(0, 100000) count — 1.17s; range(0, 400000) count — 4.3s; range(0, 4000000) count — 95s (superlinear: ~24µs/cell).
- eu -S on range(0, 400000) count: 45.2M ticks (~113/cell), 9.6M allocs (~24/cell), 9 collections, Mark 1.38s, Blocks Recycled 0, Peak Blocks 26,937.
- Same shape for iterate(+ 1, 0) take(400000) count (4.27s, Recycled 0) and range(0, 400000) foldl(+, 0) (4.09s, Recycled 0).

Blocks Recycled 0 with peak blocks growing with n suggests the consumed list prefix stays reachable (space leak), so each GC marks an ever larger live set.

Lane diagnosis so far (measured-single): not a regression (5aa27b7, before #1247/#1242, is the same); the list itself is retained; ~113 ticks/cell is the normal shape and the superlinear part is GC mark on a growing live set; triggered by advancing a list while calling a function-valued parameter (count/foldl-strict via op) — a global callee, no call, or a counter runs in constant space. Exact pinning root not yet found.

AoC risk: any puzzle walking a few million list cells takes minutes. Found by the AoC 2026 solutions-repository lane.

title: PANIC (wasm32): arr.zeros with a large dimension passes shape validation, then panics with Vec capacity overflow
description: Found by the eu-oaz72.96 lane (#1180). On wasm32, arr.zeros[300000000] passes validate_shape (cap 536,870,911 elements) and then panics in Vec allocation (capacity overflow); also on master before #1180. Fix: cap at min(MAX_ALLOC_SIZE, isize::MAX)/8 for the target (array.rs:765) and return ArrayTooLarge. Panics are P1 under CLAUDE.md: convert to an error, with a regression test (fault-injection verified).
close_reason: Fixed in #1182 (merged): element cap is min(MAX_ALLOC_SIZE, isize::MAX)/8; ArrayTooLarge on wasm32 instead of capacity-overflow panic. Unit + wasm_bindgen_test regression tests, fault-injection verified.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design: the cap MAX_ARRAY_ELEMENTS = MAX_ALLOC_SIZE/8 ignores Rust's own allocation limit (a Vec/Layout may not exceed isize::MAX bytes). On 64-bit MAX_ALLOC_SIZE (u32::MAX) is the binding limit; on wasm32 isize::MAX (2^31-1) is, so shapes between 268,435,455 and 536,870,911 elements pass validation and hit 'capacity overflow' in ndarray's vec allocation. Fix: compute the cap via a const fn element_limit(max_alloc, isize_max) = min(max_alloc, isize_max)/size_of::<f64>() and use it for MAX_ARRAY_ELEMENTS (native value unchanged). Tests: unit test of element_limit with wasm32 parameters (u32::MAX, i32::MAX) => 268,435,455, plus a wasm_bindgen_test in src/wasm.rs evaluating arr.zeros[300000000] and expecting success:false with the too-large error rather than a panic. Fault-inject by dropping the min. Native harness behaviour unchanged, so no new .eu harness test can gate this; out of scope: OOM abort for allocations under the cap that the wasm heap cannot satisfy (handle_alloc_error, not a panic).

title: (BUG) PANIC: arr.zeros with a huge dimension panics inside ndarray
description: Found by the eu-oaz72.88 lane (PR #1177), present on master: arr.zeros([100000000000000000000.0]) panics inside the ndarray crate instead of raising a eucalypt error. CLAUDE.md: panics are critical. Convert to a proper ExecutionError (naming the function and the dimension) for any dimension or shape that ndarray can't allocate (overflowing product, too large, negative or non-integer), and audit the other arr.* constructors (arr.fill, arr.from-list, reshape and so on) for the same unchecked shape arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria: No arr.* constructor panics on any numeric shape; each bad shape gives a named eucalypt error; error fixture(s) plus a regression test, fault-injection verified.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1180 (merged 9f2cc83): arr.* shapes are validated before ndarray; fault-injection verified; two independent reviews passed.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design (PR #1180): arr.zeros/fill/from-flat/reshape read their shape through validate_shape (src/eval/stg/array.rs) before ndarray is called. A non-finite or fractional dimension gives ArrayNonIntegerIndex (the same variant as #1177), a negative one ArrayNegativeIndex, and one where the checked product of the non-zero axes exceeds MAX_ALLOC_SIZE/8 (the heap's largest object) gives ArrayTooLarge, naming the function. arr.neighbours offset addition uses checked_add. Error fixtures tests/harness/errors/276_array_shape_*; fault-injection verified.

title: (BUG) string? is false for computed strings (ISSTRING checks only the boxed form)
description: Found by the eu-oaz72.58 lane (PR #1174). ISSTRING recognises only the boxed string representation, so ("a" ++ "b") string? is false, and other computed strings may be too: a silent wrong answer to a type test. #1174 fixes the same bug in number? (ISNUMBER, src/eval/stg/list.rs) for arithmetic results. Audit every IS* predicate intrinsic (string?, number?, symbol?, bool?, block?, list?, ...) against every runtime representation of its type.
design:
Audit (master fce2781): probed every IS* predicate (string?, number?, symbol?, bool?, block?, list?, datetime?, type-data?) against literal, intrinsic-computed, interpolated, set/vec/dict-extracted, metadata-carrying and imported (YAML, JSON, JSONL, TOML, EDN, CSV) values, plus io.args/io.env.
Findings: only number? misclassifies reachable values (bare-native arithmetic results) — fixed by #1174 (eu-oaz72.58). The bead's example ("a" ++ "b") is list append, not concatenation, so it is not a string; "x{1}" is a positional string anaphor (a function). Every user-reachable string/symbol/datetime is boxed by the intrinsic wrapper (wrap.rs boxes by declared return type; STR/JOIN/FMT custom wrappers box), so string?/symbol?/datetime? are correct today. bool/list/block have no native representation.
Fix: bare natives are still a valid runtime representation (Native::Str/Sym/Zdt via machine_return_* when a wrapper does not box), so ISSTRING/ISSYMBOL/ISZDT fall back to value_native when the value has no data tag — the same pattern #1174 uses for ISNUMBER, leaving ISNUMBER to #1174 to avoid conflicts.
Tests: STG unit tests in list.rs feed bare and boxed natives directly (fault-injected); harness target test-representations in 126_type_predicates.eu guards computed/imported cases for all six non-number predicates.
acceptance_criteria: Each type predicate is true for every runtime representation of its type (literal, computed, imported, unboxed and boxed); harness checks in the predicates topic file, fault-injection verified, in blob and source mode.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1178 (merged): ISSTRING/ISSYMBOL/ISZDT accept bare natives; audit found number? (eu-oaz72.58, #1174) the only user-visible misclassification.

title: (BUG) Dot lookup on a block parameter re-evaluates the field on every access instead of sharing it (~15x slower than lookup)
description: Found by the external lane (AoC 2026 solutions scaffolding). In f(b, i): b.x, mapped over a list, the field expression is re-evaluated on every call; b lookup(:x) is fast, and so is const(blk.x). eu dump inlined shows the field expression inlined at the use site rather than shared. Same family as eu-oaz72.48 and .41 (lost sharing). Minimal repro: a block whose field is expensive, passed to a function that reads it with . in a map over 1e4 elements; compare ticks (-S) of b.x and b lookup(:x). Use eu dump inlined / demands to find the pass that duplicates the work.
design: Repro: blk: { x: range(0,20000) sum }, f(b,i): b.x + i, range(0,100) map(f(blk)) sum: 13.6 s vs 0.14 s for b lookup(:x). Core, demands (x Lazy Multi) and STG (one shared x thunk in the block; one lookup ✳0 . :x in f) are all correct, so no core pass duplicates work. Cause is the engine: bc_lookup_in_block (Op::LookupLit fast path and the LookupLitForce continuation) resolves the pair's value ref and returns a copy of the field's unevaluated thunk closure; forcing the copy updates nothing, so the block's slot stays unevaluated and every .key recomputes it. Same mechanism eu-oaz72.36/.48 fixed in env_from_data_args_copy (PR #1147). Fix: when the resolved value is an update thunk, return a lazy alias closure over the value's OP_ATOM node in the pair's env (peek_code_ref for pre-decode), so forcing enters, black-holes and updates the original slot. lookup(:x) was fast because it destructures the pair via case (shared env path). Test: harness tick gate in harness_test.rs, fault-injected, blob + --source-prelude, both dispatch paths.
acceptance_criteria: b.x on a block parameter evaluates the field at most once per block (ticks within 10% of lookup on the repro); a gating harness check counts evaluations (e.g. via a side-effect-free tick bound or trace), fault-injection verified, in blob and source mode.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1175 (merged): bc_lookup_in_block returned a copy of an unevaluated field thunk, so each .key read recomputed it; it now hands out an OP_ATOM alias via share_unevaluated (shared with env_from_data_args_copy). Gated by test 236 target dot-lookup (tick budget), fault-injection verified in blob and source modes. The LookupLit fast path calls the same function but has no gating test (no shape found that reaches it and lost sharing on master).

title: Derive prelude demand signatures at blob build, stored per global slot; delete the hand table
description: From the eu-oaz72.75 design review, recommendation step 2. Report: docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-prelude-demand-signatures-design.md (PR #1170, eu-oaz72.75). Run the same demand analysis on the prelude when the blob is compiled, store the signatures in the blob keyed by global slot, and delete build_prelude_signatures. Removes drift and serves alternative preludes. Blob wire format change: two independent rig-reviews. OWNER DECISION 2026-11-13 (tracking issue decision 17): all three steps of the #1170 report accepted; this bead (step 2) dispatched immediately, P1.
design:
Design (step 2 of docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-prelude-demand-signatures-design.md):

1. xtask prelude-compile: after fuse_destructure, run split_letrecs on a copy of the merged prelude core (as source mode does before analysis) and analyse_demands over it. Walk the analysed top-level Let/Meta chain (same shape peel_all_let_bindings walks) and, for each binding whose RHS peels to a Lam, take that Lam's signature from the pointer-keyed SignatureTable, i.e. per binder, not the name-merged table. Names that occur more than once at top level get no signature. Map name -> slot via name_to_slot; result: demand_signatures: Vec<Option<Vec<Demand>>> parallel to binding_entries.
2. Compile the blob's own bodies with these signatures (intra-prelude Var::Free calls), so intra-prelude calls use the same analysis source mode does.
3. Blob: new trailing PreludeBlob field demand_signatures (#[serde(default)]); BYTECODE_WIRE_FORMAT_VERSION 9 -> 10; blob_source_hash also absorbs src/core/analyse_demand.rs and src/core/demand.rs (DEMAND_ANALYSIS_PATHS, in BUILD_RERUN_PATHS) so a blob built by an older analysis is stale, not misread.
4. Compiler: prelude_demand_sigs becomes slot-indexed (StgSettings.prelude_demand_sigs, Arc<Vec<Option<sig>>>), filled from the blob in driver/eval.rs. Lookup scoped by callee identity: Var::Bound -> user (name) table; Var::Free -> the slot of the global it resolves to; intrinsic -> intrinsic table. Delete build_prelude_signatures.
5. Intrinsic signatures unchanged. No alias/partial-application propagation (optional in the report; follow-up).
6. Tests: report §2.2/§2.3 repro programs as gating checks in tests/harness/165_demand_annotation.eu (both prelude modes via blob-mode tests), fault-injected; unit test that the blob carries signatures and that they are no stricter than source-mode named signatures. Bench ticks/stack 015-022 under the protocol, measured-single.
acceptance_criteria: No hand-written prelude signature table remains; blob and source modes agree on the report's repro set; blob format versioned; two reviews.

title: Design review: source of prelude demand signatures (hand-written table vs derived)
description:
Owner request 2026-11-13: a design review of where prelude demand (strictness) signatures come from. Today src/core/analyse_demand.rs build_prelude_signatures() (about line 207 at b8bfb43) is a hand-written table of prelude function names to DemandSignature, used by the STG compiler (src/eval/stg/compiler.rs ~1665) because blob-mode prelude functions are globals with no demand analysis. ambiguous_names() drops a name program-wide when a user binding shares it.

Owner's concerns:
- Aliasing: a user (or the prelude) binding another name to a prelude function, or shadowing one; lookup is by name, not by binding identity.
- Alternative preludes (future): the table hard-codes one prelude's names.
- Drift: when prelude definitions change, the table silently goes out of date. eu-oaz72.72 found wrong entries for repeat and iterate, and the #1158 reviews found entries longer than the binding's arity (mapcat, sort-by-num, zip).

Deliverable: a design report in docs/superpowers/reports/ (dated 2026-11-13) that measures how the current scheme behaves (concrete failure cases for aliasing, shadowing and drift, each shown with a small .eu program, in blob mode and in source mode). It should also evaluate alternatives, for example:
(a) derive signatures by running demand analysis on the prelude when the blob is compiled, and store them in the blob, keyed by global;
(b) declare strictness in prelude metadata next to each definition;
(c) keep a table but generate it, or check it in CI against source-mode analysis;
(d) key by binding identity (global/de Bruijn), not by name.
Cover correctness (never stricter than the definition), interaction with intrinsic signatures, the blob wire format (a sensitive area), performance and effort, and give a recommendation with a migration path. Design only: no implementation in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Report merged-ready in docs/superpowers/reports/ with reproduced failure cases, the alternatives compared, and a recommendation plus migration path; PR left open for the owner; follow-up implementation beads proposed to the coordinator.
close_reason: Design report merged by the owner in #1170; all three steps accepted (decision 17): .76 and .77 done, .66 open (P3).

title: (BUG) A loop threading a dict retains old versions unless the stored values are evaluated scalars
description: From dict PR 2 (#1159), owner 2026-11-12: accepted for now, but this needs attention. A recursive loop or fold that threads a dict through its iterations keeps earlier dict versions reachable when the stored values are unevaluated thunks or constructors over the old frame, so memory grows with the iteration count instead of staying bounded. Eu-oaz72.21 asks for bounded memory. The reviewers' suggested direction: memo_cell should rebuild evaluated constructors over a fresh frame, so stored values stop pinning the environment that built the previous version. Recorded as a limit in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-dict-design.md §12. GC/memory area: eucalypt-backend skill, two independent rig-reviews. Starts after #1159 merges.
design: memo_cell (src/eval/bytecode/machine.rs) generalises its boxed-scalar rebuild: an evaluated data constructor is rebuilt over fresh frames (parent root_env) field by field, recursively, following OP_ATOM aliases at each field. All or nothing: if any reachable field is not a native or an evaluated constructor (a thunk, lambda, partial application, cell), or the value exceeds a node budget (64 constructors), the original is stored unchanged, since that field would pin the caller's frame anyway and copying would be wasted. Nullary constructors over root_env are kept as they are. Never forces; observationally identical (immutable evaluated data). Unevaluated values keep their environment (laziness), as design note §12 records; the note is updated. Gate: 250_dict.eu gains a chain storing [i, i] and {a: i}-style values, peak-blocks gated in harness_test.rs, plus a 1e6-iteration run under a small --heap-limit-mib.
acceptance_criteria: A loop of 1e6 iterations that threads a dict, storing computed (non-scalar) values, runs in bounded memory (harness gate under a small --heap-limit-mib, fault-injection verified); errors corpus unchanged in both prelude modes.
close_reason: Merged in PR #1168 (merge of master re-verified and reviewed; trace-label trade-off is follow-up eu-oaz72.83)

Blocks and lazy fields remain undetached (design note §12).

title: (BUG) Prelude demand signatures for repeat and iterate are wrong on master
description: Found by the round-3 rig-review of PR #1158 (comment https://github.com/curvelogic/eucalypt/pull/1158#issuecomment-6840365215). The demand signatures recorded for prelude repeat and iterate are wrong on master, independent of #1158. A signature that claims more strictness than the function has can force a value the program never needs: a wrong result, a spurious error, or divergence on a correct lazy program (e.g. iterate's seed or repeat's value being forced). Confirm each signature against the definition, fix the analysis or the recorded signature, and audit the other prelude loop signatures for the same mistake. Also from that review, non-blocking: ambiguous_names drops a prelude name's signature program-wide whenever any binding shares the name (e.g. a block key 'map'); narrow it to the binding's scope. eucalypt-frontend skill (src/core/analyse_demand.rs).
design: Audit of build_prelude_signatures (src/core/analyse_demand.rs) against lib/prelude.eu. An arg is sm only if a saturated call evaluated to WHNF always forces it. Too-strict entries fixed: map/filter/take-while/drop-while/group-consecutive-by/over-sliding-pairs fn; map2/zip-with fn+2nd list; zip 2nd; take list; append/interleave 2nd; snoc elem; mapcat/sort-by-num/sort-by-str (arity 1, fn lazy); cross fn+ys; sort-by key+cmp; group-by/discriminate both; compose/flip data args; when fn+value; has block; deep-find key; deep-transform data; head-or/tail-or default; repeat; iterate. Deliberate exceptions kept strict as on master, documented: foldl acc and iota start (the blob's own recursion takes these signatures; lazy iota gives O(n) stack, lazy foldl changes error traces). Compiler (ProtoAppGroup::take_syntax): a Var::Bound callee takes only analysed signatures, a Var::Free callee (blob prelude global) only the prelude table, so a user binding sharing a prelude name no longer leaks either way and ambiguous_names no longer hides prelude signatures (the non-blocking #1158 note). Harness: test-prelude-laziness in 165_demand_annotation.eu, saturated calls only (pipelines are partial applications).

title: (BUG) Prelude loops (foldl etc.) compiled with suppress_inlining still call the global if: 154 ticks/elem and O(n) stack
description: Found by eu-oaz72.34 (PR #1140, merged): user then-loops are now constant-stack, but prelude loops (foldl and friends) are compiled with suppress_inlining from un-inlined bodies, so they still call the global if instead of an inlined case: foldl costs ~154 ticks/element with a ~2e6-frame stack at 1e6 (measured-single). This keeps the stack pinning the heap, so eu-oaz72.4's acceptance measurements need it alongside eu-oaz72.27 (the lazy-accumulator stack is .27's part). Fix the prelude compile path (xtask prelude-compile and the from-source fallback) so the prelude's own loops get the same if/then inlining as user code; verify blob and source paths agree. Perf figures under docs/superpowers/engine-ab/PROTOCOL.md with a confidence label; EU_PP_THRESHOLD=999999999.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1149 (merged): blob prelude bindings resolve intrinsic aliases; foldl(+) 154->128 ticks/elem at 1e6, blob sum/count max stack 1e6->9. Remaining O(n) stack is the lazy accumulator (eu-oaz72.27); source-mode sum/count/foldl(snd) O(n) stack reported to the coordinator.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design (implementation in progress): root cause is blob-only. Source mode already inlines IF into prelude foldl (108 ticks/elem for foldl(+) at 1e6). xtask prelude-compile skipped the core inline pass (to keep one form per binding) and compiled with suppress_inlining=true, so blob foldl called global if with thunked branches (154 ticks/elem). Fix in xtask only: per binding, run reduce::inline_pass over the body with the blob's inlinable combinator set bound in a Let (own name excluded so recursion stays a global call), fuse, reopen the Let so unreduced refs go back to globals; compile with suppress_inlining=false like user code. No wire-format change, no prelude source change. Max stack 2e6 at 1e6 is the lazy accumulator (eu-oaz72.27): foldl with a non-chaining op runs at max stack 10 before and after. Tradeoff: blob 608KB -> 1086KB, eager predecode makes trivial-program startup ~+20% instructions (callgrind, measured-single).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: PR #1149 (alias-only variant: per-binding core inline pass with bare intrinsic aliases, wrapper inlining on). Two rig-review passes (9e28a47, 735f795); both merges were blocked by master moving. Head 95f9982 merges master again (window fixtures re-blessed, 30->34 DIVERGENCE rows, all extra blob-mode 'called from here' labels). Needs a merge-only re-review. foldl(+) 1e6: 154->128 ticks/elem, max stack 2,000,004->2,000,003 (lazy accumulator = eu-oaz72.27); blob sum/count max stack 1,000,009->9. Source mode sum/count/foldl(snd) still O(n) stack.

title: (BUG) eu test FILE | head -1 panics on a broken pipe (tester run_plans print!)
description: Found by the eu-oaz72.35 lane (2026-11-12): piping `eu test FILE` into `head -1` panics with a broken pipe, because src/driver/tester.rs (run_plans) writes with print!, which panics on EPIPE. A panic in user-reachable code is P1 under CLAUDE.md. Fix: write through a handle and treat BrokenPipe as a clean exit; audit other print!/println! in src/driver and src/bin for the same. Regression test required, fault-injection verified. (Originally filed locally as eu-oaz72.39; that id went to the security-alert bead.)
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1141 (merged)

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design and outcome (PR #1141, merged): every stdout write the CLI makes itself (tester, eu dump phases, list-targets, doc, fmt, error, --explain/help) now goes through std::io::Write instead of print!/println!. A closed pipe exits 0 silently via EucalyptError::is_broken_pipe at the eu.rs boundary; the eval dumps map EPIPE to OutputStreamClosed. The tester drops EPIPE on its progress lines (stdout_ok), so the suite still runs to completion and reports its real verdict: a failing suite exits 1. Other write failures are still reported. No SIGPIPE handler, because it would affect io.shell. Tests: tests/broken_pipe_test.rs (11 commands, plus a failing suite under a closed pipe), both fault-injection verified. Noted, not fixed: eu test a.eu b.eu runs only the last input.

title: (BUG) drop, split-at, rotate and nth test n zero?: negative counts fail or never terminate on infinite lists
description: Follow-up from eu-oaz72.35 (PR #1136). take now stops at n <= 0, but drop, split-at/rotate and nth still test `n zero?` in lib/prelude.eu: a negative count makes drop fail on tail [], and split-at and nth(-1) never terminate on infinite lists. Same family as eu-oaz72.35 (hang). Decide and document behaviour for negative counts consistent with take (drop(-k) = identity, split-at(-k) = [[], xs]; nth(-1) an error, not a hang). Reviewer also noted take(0.5) now yields 1 element: decide whether non-integer counts are an error. Prelude edit: small; serialised review slot. Regression tests fault-injection verified.
design: drop, split-at: stop at n <= 0 (as take since eu-oaz72.35), so drop(n<=0)=l, split-at(n<=0)=[[],l], rotate(n<=0)=l. nth and update-nth: a negative numeric index panics 'index {n} out of range: list indices start at 0', checked once before the walk and guarded by number? so a misapplied nth(list, 0) keeps its existing diagnostic. Non-integer counts: behaviour left as is and documented as 'not rejected'; decision left to the owner (open question). PR #1144.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1144 (merged). Non-integer count decision left open for the owner; see comment.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design (PR #1143): in analyse_demand.rs, Block field values and List elements go through constructor_env: strictness Lazy (a constructor does not evaluate its contents) and AtMostOnce raised to Multi (the structure can be read many times; AtMostOnce skipped the update frame and recomputed on each read). Exception: the root unit's block (followed through Let/Meta bodies) keeps strict fields, since RENDER_DOC forces them; a block literal is a Let with a Block body, so a Block body alone is not evidence of rendering. Making every block lazy changed 34 diagnostics snapshots; with the root exception none change. Round 1 found lost sharing, caused by the engine defect eu-oaz72.48 (fixed by #1147). The {m: slow(n)}.([m]) case is fixed here via Multi (test 239, tick-gated). {a: panic("x") b: 1}.b already passes on master after #1147. title: (BUG) Binding captured by a lambda is recomputed on every call (captured variable left AtMostOnce, update elided)
description: Found in review of eu-oaz72.1 (PR #1135, comment 6826084013); also on master before #1135. `b: ds sum` used inside `h(x)` and h called 6 times takes 56.1M ticks against 22.4M for 1 call (measured-single, not under protocol). Likely cause: analyse_lam leaves captured variables AtMostOnce, so their thunk update is elided and the work repeats per call. Loss of sharing, same family as eu-oaz72.36; relevant to eu-oaz72.27 (strict accumulators). Fix must restore sharing for captured variables (cardinality Many when captured by a lambda that may be applied more than once). Perf claims under docs/superpowers/engine-ab/PROTOCOL.md.
design:
Repro: f6(ds): { b: ds sum  h(x): x + b }.(h(1)+...+h(6)) costs 5.4M ticks vs 2.0M for one call; eu dump demands shows h Multi, b AtMostOnce. (Block-body and map forms are masked by the eu-oaz72.40 constructor fixup.)
Cause: analyse_lam returns the body's free-variable demands unchanged. A lambda value may be applied any number of times and each application evaluates its body, so a captured variable's syntactic AtMostOnce is wrong; analyse_let then passes the Lam RHS's cardinality through unscaled ('an updated thunk evaluates its RHS once' holds for a thunk, not for a Lam body).
Fix: analyse_lam raises captured AtMostOnce to Multi (strictness unchanged — out of scope). Exception: a lambda literal applied directly in an App (beta-redex) is one-shot, so analyse_app analyses it without the raise. Update the analyse_let comment.
Tests: unit tests (captured -> Multi; beta-redex stays AtMostOnce); harness test with a tick gate in harness_test.rs (six calls cost about one fold), fault-injected.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1156 (merged): captured variables of a lambda value are Multi; beta-redex exception only for full application. Test 240 gates by ticks.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: PR #1156. Fix: analyse_lam raises captured AtMostOnce to Multi; beta-redex keeps cardinality. Note for follow-up (not filed): strictness still flows out of a lambda body unscaled, so a captured variable can be Strict though the lambda may never be applied; not made observable in probes (g(ds): { b: ds max-of h(x): x + b }.(h) then g([]) unapplied did not error).

title: range(b, e) with e < b never terminates; take(n) with n < 0 never stops on infinite lists
description: timeout 5 eu -e 'range(10, 9) count' hangs (exit 124). [1,2,3] take(-1) returns the whole list: the count goes negative and never reaches zero, so on an infinite list (which range builds on) take(-1) never stops. Expected: range(b, e) with e <= b is the empty list (as in Python/Clojure); take(n) with n <= 0 is []. Impact: AoC 2025 day10 part 2 (examples/aoc25/day10.eu inner-solve) calls range(lo, hi + 1) with lo > hi on 26 of 185 machines and runs for minutes into GB of memory instead of skipping them; with a guard, 181 machines finish in under 2 s each. Taking an empty range for e <= b is arguably a semantic change for a case that currently does not terminate; record the decision in the PR.
design: Change take's stop test from (n zero?) to (n <= 0): take(n) with n <= 0 is [] and the count can no longer skip past zero (negative or fractional n). range(b, e) is ints-from(b) take(e - b), so e <= b gives [] with no change to range itself. Treated as a bug fix: the old behaviour for these inputs was non-termination (infinite list) or returning the whole list (finite list), neither intended; matches Python/Clojure. drop and split-at keep their (n zero?) tests (out of scope; noted in PR). Docs: update take and range doc strings, regenerate docs/reference/prelude and lib/prelude.blob. Tests: new harness file covering range(10,9), range(5,5), take(-1)/take(0) on finite and infinite lists, fault-injected by reverting the take change.
acceptance_criteria: range(10, 9), range(5, 5) and take(-1) / take(0) give []; harness tests incl. an infinite-list take(-1); day10 part 2 no longer hangs on reversed bounds; fault-injection verified.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1136 (merged): take(n) with n <= 0 is [], so range(b, e) with e <= b is []. Harness test 232, fault-injection verified. Left for follow-up: drop, split-at and nth still test n zero?, so a negative count still misbehaves in them.

title: Lists built by foldr (incl. prelude filter) lose sharing and are recomputed on every traversal
description:
Repro (rep6.eu):
  slow(y): range(0, 5000) map(_ * 2) foldl(+, y)
  p?(y): slow(y) > 0
  xs: range(0, 20) filter(p?)
then target one: xs sum -> 15.6M ticks; target two: (xs sum) + (xs sum) -> 30.4M ticks, i.e. xs's elements are recomputed on the second traversal. Same with ws: foldr({x: • a: •}.cons(slow(x), a), [], l). map keeps sharing. eu dump stg shows the if else-branch closures let-bound without 'thunk', so not updatable and re-entered on each force. Lazy semantics require call-by-need sharing; this is a laziness/memoisation bug (cf. closed eu-bc34x, eu-xxrx). Impact: AoC 2025 day09 (insert-gaps foldr: each lvs !! 1 re-runs xsect, ~24k ticks per access) and day10 part 2 (frees recomputed). May share a root cause with the if/then tail-position bug (eu-oaz72.34) - fix and test independently.
design:
Root cause (found 2026-11-12): not specific to foldr or if. A constructor whose field refers beyond its own immediate env frame loses sharing for that field. Minimal repro: f(x, a): cons(slow(x), a); k: f(1, []) -- (k sum)+(k sum) costs 2x. The STG optimiser strips alias lets, so CONS(slow(x), a) compiles to `λ{2} let [0] thunk slow(x) in Cons(✳0, ✳2)`: ✳2 is in the arg frame. When a case destructures the value, env_from_data_args (bytecode machine) shares the constructor's backing only if every field is in the immediate frame; otherwise (deeper local, global, >4 fields) env_from_data_args_copy copies each field's raw value into a fresh frame. An unevaluated update thunk is thus duplicated: forcing it updates the copy, the original slot stays unevaluated, and every later traversal (each re-entry of the Cons copies again) recomputes it. filter (foldr + lambda building cons(x, xs)) and any foldr op that calls a cons-building function hit this; map / direct cons(...) recursion keep sharing because their Cons fields are all immediate.

Function arguments already avoid this: make_arg_array passes an OP_ATOM alias closure over the caller frame for an unsettled local (eu-wpswc). Fix: do the same in env_from_data_args_copy -- for a Local field whose slot holds an update thunk, bind an alias closure over the field's OP_ATOM node and the constructor's env instead of the raw thunk, so forcing it enters (black-holes, updates) the original slot. Evaluated values are still copied directly. Needs the Cons args' atom code refs in both dispatch modes: byte mode has them (arg offsets); predecode keeps an ordinal run for Cons args in the offsets pool (instr.b) alongside the refs run.

Relationship to eu-oaz72.34: independent. That bug was stack growth from if/then loop structure (inliner); this is a data-field copy in the engine. The un-updatable if-branch closures noted in the bead are a red herring: they are entered at most once per call and are not the lost sharing.

Test: harness test counting ticks? Prefer a trace-free gate: compare (xs sum)+(xs sum) against 2*(xs sum) is value-equal, so gate on evaluation count via io? Plan: harness test using a side-effect-free counter is impossible; use -S tick budget is not gateable from .eu. Will use a Rust test in tests/ or harness bench-style assertion -- decide after checking the tester's facilities.
acceptance_criteria: two costs ~1x one (within a small constant) for filter and foldr-built lists; harness regression test asserting tick counts or a trace-count of slow evaluations; fault-injection verified; root cause recorded, with the relationship to eu-oaz72.34.
notes: PR #1147: engine fix (env_from_data_args_copy aliases unevaluated thunks) + demand fix (alias bindings pass cardinality). Harness 234, fault-injection verified. Report docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-12-foldr-sharing.md.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1147 (merged): engine env_from_data_args_copy aliases unevaluated thunks; demand analysis passes alias cardinality on. Gated by harness 236, fault-injection verified. Root cause and relationship to eu-oaz72.34 (independent) in docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-12-foldr-sharing.md.

title: Loops through if/then use O(n) stack and 50-75 ticks per iteration (recursive branch allocated as a thunk)
description:
Measured 2026-11-12 (eu -S, one run each, measured-single), 1e6 iterations:
- A lazy(i, a): if(i = 0, a, lazy(i - 1, a + 1)) -> 52 ticks/iter, Max Stack 3,000,001, 3.3 s
- B same with a forced in the condition (if(a < 0 ∨ i = 0, ...)) -> 75 ticks/iter, Max Stack 1,000,008, 3.6 s
- C range(0, n) foldl(+, 0) -> 163 ticks/element, Max Stack 3,000,004, 8.3 s
- D as A using then -> 61 ticks/iter, Max Stack 3,000,001
Even with a strict accumulator (B) the stack grows one frame per iteration, so no self-recursive loop runs in constant stack. Hypothesis (CONFIRM FIRST with eu dump stg / dump runtime): if is the intrinsic __IF (lib/prelude.eu:273; then(t, f, c) is if(c, t, f)), and its branch arguments are compiled as lazy arguments, so the recursive call is allocated as a thunk and forcing it pushes an update frame each step. Proposed fix: compile saturated calls of the prelude's __IF (and so then) as a case on the condition with the branches in tail position, no branch thunks.
Semantics: intended as a pure bug/performance fix - values, termination, errors and trace/▶ ordering unchanged; the unchosen branch is never evaluated; applies only to saturated calls of the real __IF (not when if is passed as a value, partially applied or shadowed). Error traces may show fewer if frames (diagnostic shape only). If the confirmed root cause differs, re-assess the no-semantic-change claim before fixing.
Separate: lazy accumulators (A vs B, two extra frames/iter) and foldl laziness are eu-oaz72.27. GC (0 collections, ~2 GB per 1e6 steps) is eu-oaz72.4.
design:
Root cause (confirmed 2026-11-12 with eu dump inlined/stg on master 362ef55): the bead's hypothesis does not hold. A saturated IF is already inlined as 'case c of True/False' and the branch binding is a non-updatable value, so loop B (if, strict accumulator) already runs in constant stack (Max Stack 8). The O(n) stack is in loops through 'then': catenation makes 'c then(t, f)' the curried App(App(then,[t,f]),[c]); beta_reduce only reduces an application whose own argument list saturates the lambda, so 'then' is never reduced, and in blob mode 'then' is not even in the inlinable set (xtask's fixed-point tags candidates before substituting intrinsic aliases, so if(c,t,f) never looks closed). Each iteration then enters the recursive call through an updatable thunk: Max Stack ~1 per iteration. A and D's remaining 2e6 stack is the lazy accumulator chain (eu-oaz72.27).
Fix: (1) beta_reduce merges a curried application of a closed-bodied inlinable lambda into one saturated application (recursive combinators such as map excluded: extending copy-specialisation to every pipeline is a separate decision, and it cost call-site labels in 5 diagnostics snapshots when tried). (2) xtask substitutes the intrinsic aliases into candidates before tagging, adding then, when, !, !=, //, //=?, assert, second, ¬ and ↑ to the blob's inlinable set (parity with the source path). A compile-time tail-position IF in the STG compiler was prototyped and dropped: with (1)+(2) it changed no tick, alloc or stack figure.
Out of scope, follow-up: the prelude's own loops (foldl, case C) are compiled with suppress_inlining from un-inlined bodies, so they still call the global 'if' (C: 160 ticks/element, 2e6 stack).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed and recorded; loop B runs in constant stack at 1e6 and 1e7 iterations; ticks/iteration for A-D reported before/after per the performance protocol (confidence labels); harness tests (incl. a deep-recursion test that would overflow without the fix) fault-injection verified; no harness output changes other than curated error traces, which are listed in the PR.
notes:
2026-11-12 from the 2025 re-analysis: self-recursion through if keeps ~2 stack frames per iteration whose environments stay live, so the stack pins the heap (ℕ map(_*2) nth(300000): Max Stack 600k, ~1 GB allocated; never finishes under 64 MiB). Every 2025 OOM case thrashes under a smaller limit for this reason, so this bug is the prerequisite for eu-oaz72.4 to pay off. Expected after .34 + .4: d08 p2 finishes in ~25-35 s, d04 p2 ~30-50 s (measure).
2026-11-12: PR #1140 (https://github.com/curvelogic/eucalypt/pull/1140). Follow-up not filed (lane touches only its own bead): prelude loops (foldl etc.) are compiled with suppress_inlining from un-inlined bodies, so they still call the global 'if'; consider inlining intrinsic aliases in xtask's STG compile of prelude bodies. 1e7 constant-stack check blocked on eu-oaz72.4 (no GC collections; heap exceeds 15 GB).
Round 2 (head 06a6c07): xtask now substitutes only the 'if' alias (adds then, when); substituting all aliases admitted //=? and moved 011_assert_pred's blob-mode primary. No diagnostics snapshot changes. Test renumbered to 233. Re-measured vs master 391e71a: D 50->37 ticks/iter, E 73->57, E Max Stack 1,000,009->8.
close_reason: Merged in PR #1140: then-loops run in constant stack (E Max Stack 1,000,009 -> 8); 1e7 check blocked on eu-oaz72.4.

title: Collection constructors: vec.of and set.of as bulk intrinsics, with from-list aliases
description:
Owner decision 2026-11-11. Make list-to-collection construction consistent in name and implementation.
- Names: `vec.of(xs)` and `set.of(xs)` are the primary constructors (both read as 'a vec/set of several elements'); `vec.from-list` and `set.from-list` exist as aliases of them, pairing with the existing `to-list` on each. str.of is out of scope (strings are a special case; a future str.from is a separate decision). arr.from-flat(shape, xs) unchanged.
- Implementation: today vec.of is the intrinsic __VEC.OF (one pass, O(n)), but set.from-list is a prelude foldl of set.add (lib/prelude.eu:1973), O(n^2) because each add copies the set: range(0, 20000) set.from-list takes 10.6 s. Add a bulk intrinsic __SET.OF (deep-force the list like VecOf in src/eval/stg/vec.rs, build once), bind set.of to it and set.from-list as its alias.
- Any future map type follows the same pattern (map.of pairs, map.from-list alias, map.to-list).
New intrinsic: owner merges. Update docs (sets and vec reference pages, cheat sheet, agent-reference), type annotations, and prelude name lists in the tree-sitter, TextMate and Emacs grammars. Note: the copy/leak behaviour of set.add itself is eu-oaz72.5 (P0).
design:
Design (implementer, 2026-11-12):
- A bulk set intrinsic already exists, unbound by the prelude: SET.FROM_LIST (src/eval/stg/set.rs, slot 94) deep-forces the list like VecOf, then one sort+dedup (O(n log n)). Rename it in place to SET.OF (same slot, so no new registry entry and no index shift). Its non-primitive error takes the call's annotation instead of Smid::default().
- Prelude: set.of: '__SET.OF'; set.from-list: of (alias, same function). vec.from-list: of (alias of '__VEC.OF'). Types [a] → any as today. select/dissoc keep calling set.from-list (now the intrinsic).
- sourcemap intrinsic→prelude-name map: SET.OF → set.of.
- Docs: regenerate prelude reference pages; sets/vec guide, cheat sheet, agent-reference mention set.of / from-list aliases.
- Editor grammar name lists NOT touched: plan §4 says feature PRs leave them to the grammar lanes (plan wins over bead text).
- Harness test: identity of names (same results), sort+dedup, mixed types, empty list, 100000-element set.size, error for non-primitive.
acceptance_criteria: set.of and set.from-list are the same function; vec.of and vec.from-list are the same function; range(0, 100000) set.of set.size runs in well under a second; set.from-list results unchanged (sorted to-list, dedup); harness tests for both names; docs and grammar name lists updated.
close_reason: Merged in PR #1155: set.of bulk intrinsic, set.from-list / vec.from-list aliases, docs. Grammar name lists left to the grammar lanes (plan §4).

title: dict: GC-native persistent ordered tree with lazy values; sets and priority queue on it
description: The largest gap for AoC: there is no map with non-string keys and sub-linear insert. Blocks take symbol keys with linear lookup (src/eval/stg/block.rs:462) and O(n) merge (2025 day 11's DP table takes ~4 s this way); sets copy on every add. Memoisation, cycle detection (state -> step), Dijkstra distances, frequency counts and 2020 d15 / 2024 d22-style puzzles all need it. Proposal: a HAMT (or similar) intrinsic keyed by primitives (ints, strings, symbols) with O(log n) assoc/dissoc/lookup, plus set operations on the same structure, and prelude wrappers (map.from-list, map.get-or, map.assoc, map.update-with, map.keys/values/entries, frequencies). New intrinsic: owner merges.

1. Name: dict (map is the prelude function).

description:

title: eu fmt --reformat and LSP formatting turn a leading unit docstring into metadata, producing an unparseable file
description:
A file that starts with a unit docstring, e.g.
  "doc"
  x: 1
becomes `` ` "doc" `` followed by `x: 1` under `eu fmt --reformat`; for examples/aoc25/day07.eu the result fails `eu check` with 'malformed declaration head' / 'empty expression'. The LSP formatting request uses the same path, so format-on-save corrupts such files. Conservative `eu fmt` is fine.
design: Root cause: Formatter::reformat_block_metadata (src/syntax/export/format.rs) emits a backtick before unit/block metadata. Unit/block metadata is a bare soup before the first declaration; a backtick makes it declaration metadata on the next declaration, so the head becomes malformed. Fix: emit the soup bare. Same family, fixed together because the acceptance requires every lib/*.eu and examples/aoc25/*.eu to reformat parse-clean and idempotently: (1) reformat_block dropped block metadata (incl. {x y} shorthand -> { }) and single-line blocks dropped declaration metadata; emit block meta, and lay a block out multi-line when any declaration carries metadata. (2) Single-line vs multi-line decisions for blocks and lists measured the ORIGINAL source text, so a second pass saw different lengths (lib/lens.eu, lib/test.eu non-idempotent). Measure the flat width of the formatted candidate instead, so layout is a function of the tree alone. LSP formatting calls the same format_source, so it is fixed by the same change. Tests: unit tests in format.rs and LSP formatting.rs (round-trip parse-clean + idempotent for leading docstring), a harness-driven test over every lib/*.eu and examples/aoc25/*.eu.
acceptance_criteria: Reformat of every examples/aoc25/*.eu and lib/*.eu is parse-clean and idempotent; regression test for a leading unit docstring.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1150 (merged): reformat keeps unit/block/decl metadata, layout idempotent and linear in nesting.

comments.text: PR #1150 opened: unit/block metadata emitted bare; block meta and in-block decl meta preserved; layout measured on formatted text (idempotent). Corpus test over lib/*.eu and examples/aoc25/*.eu, harness 235, LSP test. Not addressed: tabs inside interpolations become spaces under eu fmt (conservative path), raised in #1148 review.

title: Demand analysis forces a block binding used only in an untaken branch (prefix drop-while call)
description:
Wrong result (spurious error) on valid code; a 2025-style AoC day 3 solution now fails with 'max of empty list'.

Minimal repro (m1.eu):
  f(k, ds): { b: ds max-of  a: drop-while(!= b, ds) }.((k = 0) then([], cons(b, f(k - 1, a tail))))
  r: f(1, [3])

`timeout 30 eu m1.eu` -> error: max of empty list (trace: r -> f). Expected r: [3].
Passes with `eu run --suppress-demand-analysis m1.eu`, and passes when written in pipeline form `a: ds drop-while(!= b)`.
So demand analysis marks `b` (needed only in the else branch, via the inlined drop-while predicate) as strict when drop-while is called in prefix form. Use `eu dump demands` to locate.
design: Root cause: DemandAnalyser::analyse_let (src/core/analyse_demand.rs) propagated each non-absent binding's RHS demand env to the outer scope UNSCALED. In the prefix form, drop-while is inlined into a's RHS as 'let __shared_p? = λe. NOT(EQ(e, b)) in IF(...)'; the lambda's body env (b: Strict) leaks through the Lazy __shared_p? binding and the Lazy a binding, so the outer let marks b Strict and LetStrict forces max-of([]) in the untaken branch. The pipeline form passes because the predicate is an App argument, which analyse_app already scales by the argument demand. Fix: scale each propagated RHS free-variable demand by the binding's own demand (Demand::scale), keeping the inner recursive flag (it describes the binding, not its free variables). Effect is conservative: strictness can only drop to Lazy, cardinality only rise to Multi. Tests: harness test with prefix and pipeline forms plus nested-let variant; unit test in analyse_demand.rs; fault-inject by reverting the scaling.
acceptance_criteria: Repro above prints r: [3] with demand analysis on; harness regression test covering prefix and pipeline forms, fault-injection verified; root cause noted in the PR.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1135 (merged): analyse_let now scales propagated RHS strictness by the binding's demand. Harness test 231 + unit test, fault-injection verified.

title: Parser panic: index out of bounds at parse.rs:87 on unclosed « or ⟦ at end of file
description:
`printf '«: 1' > p.eu; timeout 10 eu p.eu` -> thread panicked at src/syntax/rowan/parse.rs:87:51: index out of bounds: the len is 4 but the index is 4 (Parser::next_range reads tokens[next_token] past the end).
Same for inputs `x: «`, `⟦`, `x: 1 ⟦`, under eu, eu check and the LSP. In the LSP the panic kills the server (rc 101), so typing « or ⟦ at the end of a buffer kills the editor's language server.
acceptance_criteria: All four inputs give a parse error diagnostic, no panic, in eu, eu check and eu lsp; regression tests (harness error test + LSP test), fault-injection verified.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1137 (merged)

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design: root cause is Parser::next_range indexing tokens[next_token] when next_token == tokens.len() (end of input). Only the unicode bracket paths (parse_bracket_expression's UnclosedBracketExpr) reach it at EOF; braces/parens use other range code. Fix next_range itself (general mechanism, covers all callers incl. expect()): at EOF return an empty TextRange at end of text. Tests: parser unit tests for the four inputs, error harness test for unclosed ⟦ at EOF, LSP diagnostics test that the server survives and reports a parse error.

title: LSP hover panics with rowan 'Bad offset' when the parse tree is shorter than the document
description:
Open a document with text (printf form):  '(M."
⌈{}⌉: { :monad bind: b }
` "N"
'  and request textDocument/hover at line 2 (0-based), character 1.
Server panics: rowan-0.15.17 cursor.rs:751 'Bad offset: range 0..38 offset 40' via lsp::hover::hover -> token_at_offset.
Two defects: hover does not clamp the offset to the tree's range, and the parse tree is shorter than the source text (error recovery drops text - the tree should be lossless). Found by fuzzing edits of tests/harness/096_monadic_blocks.eu.
design: Root cause: StringPatternLexer and CStringPatternLexer (src/syntax/rowan/string_lex.rs) skip whitespace inside a {...} interpolation without emitting a token, so the green tree is shorter than the source (repro: 38 vs 40 bytes), and the parse_string_pattern fallback arm drops unexpected tokens with next() but no sink token. LSP handlers then call token_at_offset with a document offset past the tree's end, which rowan asserts on. Fix: (1) lexers emit WHITESPACE tokens for interpolation whitespace; parse_string_interpolation_content attaches them as trivia (add_trivia) inside STRING_INTERPOLATION, so AST node children and semantics are unchanged; fallback arm emits the token. (2) Defence in depth: a single LSP helper clamps an offset to root.text_range() before token_at_offset/covering_element, used by hover, navigation (definition, references), completion, highlight and any other handler mapping a position into the tree. Tests: parser unit test that tree text == source for the repro and whitespace-in-interpolation cases; LSP hover regression test on the repro document; both fault-injection verified.
acceptance_criteria: Hover on any position in any document never panics (clamp + fix lossless recovery); parse tree text length equals document length for the repro; LSP regression test.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1148 (merged): lossless interpolation whitespace + LSP offset clamp; harness test 234.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: PR #1148 opened: lossless interpolation whitespace (string lexers emit WHITESPACE trivia) + LSP offset clamp (position_to_tree_offset) across hover/definition/completion/highlight/references/rename/selection. Harness test 234 + 3 unit tests, fault-injection verified. Side effect: eu fmt keeps whitespace inside interpolations instead of dropping it.

title: gate_liveness registers blob-gated tests against a job that never runs them; two regression tests execute in NO CI job
description:
Found by bead verification 2026-07-28, corroborated independently by two separate audits.

tests/gate_liveness.rs::every_blob_gated_file_names_a_ci_job_that_generates_a_blob asserts that the named CI job EXISTS and RUNS 'cargo xtask prelude-compile'. It never asserts that the job RUNS THE REGISTERED TARGET.

Two files are registered against 'diagnostics-blob-mode' (gate_liveness.rs:136 and :144):
  tests/harness_test.rs
  tests/wire_format_enforcement_test.rs

That job's run steps invoke only diagnostics_blame_plumbing_test, diagnostics_invariants, blob_deprecation_test and diagnostics_snapshots. Neither registered target is among them.

CONSEQUENCE — TWO REGRESSION TESTS FOR MERGED 0.14 FIXES EXECUTE NOWHERE:
  test_blob_core_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal_on_a_large_file (tests/harness_test.rs:3669) — eu-r4647's own end-to-end gate. cfg(prelude_blob_ok), so it compiles OUT of the blob-less Test Suite job, and the blob job never invokes it.
  the_embedded_blob_matches_the_inputs_on_disk (tests/wire_format_enforcement_test.rs:206) — eu-3skeg's own regression test. Identical situation.

eu-r4647 survives verification only because its UNIT gate (src/driver/check.rs:1182) is ungated and runs under plain cargo test. Its end-to-end gate is inert.

WHY THIS IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE OF THE PATTERN: gate_liveness.rs was written (eu-oxtcq / PR #1095) precisely to end the class of 'a cfg-gated file contributes zero tests and nobody notices'. This is that class, occurring INSIDE the mechanism built to stop it — the second such case after eu-l51r7. Wicket added both registry entries during the #1095 review and did not notice the job it registered them against does not execute them. That is not a criticism of wicket: the registry's API invites exactly this error, because naming a job that supplies a blob LOOKS like naming a job that runs your test.

FIX IS CHEAP: one extra assertion in every_blob_gated_file_names_a_ci_job_that_generates_a_blob — that the named job's body also mentions the registered target. Consider also folding in the engine-matrix requirement from eu-l51r7, since both are the same missing idea: the registry records that a supplier exists, not what the supplier actually covers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. gate_liveness asserts that each registered blob-gated file names a CI job whose body actually INVOKES that target, not merely one that generates a blob. Fault-injection verified: point a registry entry at a job that supplies a blob but does not run the target, and the gate must fail naming the file.
2. tests/harness_test.rs and tests/wire_format_enforcement_test.rs are actually executed under a blob in CI, OR their registry entries are corrected to name a job that does run them.
3. Confirm no OTHER registry entry has the same defect — enumerate every entry against its named job's run steps and record the result.
notes: Related: eu-l51r7 (same missing idea, engine axis rather than target axis), eu-oxtcq (the audit that should have caught this class), eu-3skeg and eu-r4647 (the two fixes whose end-to-end gates are inert).
close_reason: Fixed: gate_liveness now asserts the supplier job runs the target; blob-mode-tests.sh reaches harness_test and wire_format_enforcement_test via cfg(prelude_blob_ok)
