title: EDN export emits BigInt literals that eu's own EDN importer rejects
description:
Introduced by the eu-1tkk.7.23 fix (PR #1091/#1096, merged c21e6d72). Found by bead verification 2026-07-28, confirmed independently by the coordinator by reading master 45a4c268.

BEFORE: 'eu -x edn' on an integer above i64::MAX silently CORRUPTED it - 9999999999999999999 exported as 10000000000000000000, no error, exit 0. That was the defect eu-1tkk.7.23 fixed, and fixing it was right.

AFTER: src/export/edn.rs:34 emits Value::BigInt, which edn_format renders with an N suffix - '9999999999999999999N'. Exact digits, no corruption. Good.

THE ASYMMETRY: src/import/edn.rs rejects Value::BigInt outright -

  Value::BigInt(i) => Err(SourceError::InvalidNumber(i.to_string(), file_id, Span::default())),

So eu now EMITS EDN THAT EU ITSELF CANNOT READ. Export and import disagree about the language.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT: the bead's acceptance criterion said 'with a harness fixture asserting the exact digits round-trip'. Fixture 213_edn_large_integer.eu asserts the exact emitted digits and was fault-injection verified - but it never re-imports. The criterion reads equally as 'the exported digits are exact' (delivered) and 'the value survives export-then-import' (not delivered), so a fixture could satisfy it while the round trip remained impossible. Neither the author's PR nor wicket's review (wicket-014-review-1091.md) mentions the importer.

SEVERITY IS A JUDGEMENT CALL AND THE OWNER SHOULD MAKE IT. Argument for P1: a data tool that emits a format it cannot re-read is a fidelity defect of the same family as the corruption it replaced, and 'eu -x edn > f.edn' followed by re-import is an ordinary workflow. Argument for lower: the pre-fix behaviour was strictly worse (silent corruption beats a loud rejection), the affected range is integers above i64::MAX only, and the rejection is a clear diagnostic rather than a wrong answer. Filed P1 so it is not lost; downgrade freely.
acceptance_criteria:
Either:
(a) src/import/edn.rs accepts Value::BigInt and maps it to the same eucalypt value the exporter started from, with a harness fixture that performs a genuine ROUND TRIP - export to EDN, re-import the emitted text, assert the recovered value equals the original - fault-injection verified by breaking the import arm; OR
(b) an explicit written decision that eucalypt EDN export is deliberately not re-importable above i64::MAX, recorded in docs/reference/ and the CHANGELOG, with 213_edn_large_integer.eu extended to pin the rejection so the asymmetry cannot silently change.

Do NOT close by tightening the fixture's wording alone. The original criterion was ambiguous between two readings and that ambiguity is what let this through.
notes: Related: eu-1tkk.7.23 should NOT be closed as VERIFIED while this stands - it is PARTIAL. See also the sibling finding that the entire export family (eu-1tkk.7.20/.23/.24/.25/.28, eu-1z503) landed with zero CHANGELOG entries despite two user-visible breaking behaviour changes.

title: the ~500 non-error harness tests run in-process and never exercise src/bin/eu.rs
description:
Found by clarion during the eu-oxtcq gate audit, 2026-07-27, on master a1af1f0b.
Mechanism M6 of that inventory: a test that calls an entry point users do not hit.

WHAT WAS MEASURED

tests/harness_test.rs:54-56 runs an ordinary harness fixture as

    fn run_test(opt: &EucalyptOptions) {
        let exit_code = tester::test(opt).unwrap();

which goes tester::test -> tester::run_plans (src/driver/tester.rs:156) ->
InProcessTester -> driver::eval. It never spawns a binary. 506 tests are
generated from tests/harness/**, of which the ~330 non-error ones take this
in-process route. By contrast the error tests go through
tester::error_test_with_binary(eu_binary(), ..) (harness_test.rs:113) and the
typecheck tests spawn `eu check --strict` plus the eval path
(harness_test.rs:150-215), so those two families DO exercise the real binary.

WHY IT MATTERS

src/bin/eu.rs is not a thin wrapper. Lines 183-213 contain logic that exists
nowhere else:

  * the blob-core type-check dispatch --- `loader.prelude_blob()` decoded
    into prelude_units and handed to
    driver::check::run_type_checker_from_blob_core, with an explicit fallback
    to run_type_checker for a blob without baked cores. This is the ONLY
    non-test caller of run_type_checker_from_blob_core;
  * emission of the resulting type warnings to stderr via codespan_reporting.

So the largest test family in the project cannot observe either. This is the
same class as eu-vbctt (which is about `eu check` never reaching the
blob-core path) but an order of magnitude wider, and it compounds M11 /
eu-5yn9v: the harness fixtures that DO run under a blob in CI run via
`eu test tests/harness`, which does not include tests/harness/errors/** at
all, because those are generated Rust tests.

CONSEQUENCE

A regression confined to the eval-path blob-core dispatch --- a warning that
goes missing, a diagnostic sited differently, a fallback that stops firing ---
is invisible to ~330 harness tests, and the fixtures that would show it are
in the family that never runs under a blob. eu-rb5n was exactly this shape:
`065_lookup_key_typo_warns.eu` lost its warning on the eval path only, and a
dedicated single-file test had to be written for it after the fact
(test_eval_path_warns_on_record_key_typo).

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED

Coordinator ruling 2026-07-27: this is a harness-architecture change, not a
diagnostic bug, so its release status is for the owner to decide rather than
the coordinator. Filed with the measurements so that ruling can be made.

Options, roughly in increasing cost:
  1. Leave in-process as the default and add a small, explicit subprocess
     sweep over a chosen subset --- cheap, but reintroduces the allowlist
     mechanism the audit is trying to eliminate (M3).
  2. Give run_test a subprocess mode behind an env var, run it as an extra CI
     job. Measured cost is the concern: the in-process suite is ~43s; a
     process per fixture will be substantially more.
  3. Make the in-process path go through the same dispatch bin/eu.rs uses, by
     hoisting lines 183-213 of src/bin/eu.rs into a shared driver function
     both callers use. This removes the divergence rather than testing around
     it, and is the option that makes the other two unnecessary.

Related: eu-vbctt (same class, `eu check`), eu-5yn9v (blob-mode coverage is
an allowlist), eu-oxtcq (the parent audit; this is mechanism M6).

title: (BUG) blob-baked DirectApp/LookupLit Smids resolve to WRONG user source locations
description:
Found while fixing eu-1tkk.7.21.

StgArena reconstruction elides Ann nodes and Lambda-form annotations on the
blob path, because a raw Smid baked at xtask build time indexes into a
SourceMap the loading process never populated (see the Smid struct doc
comment in src/common/sourcemap.rs).

That elision does NOT cover the two inline Smids that ArenaStgSyn carries in
its own fields: DirectApp { smid, .. } and LookupLit { smid, .. }. Both are
copied through reconstruct_arena_syn verbatim
(src/eval/stg/arena.rs, the ArenaStgSyn::DirectApp and ArenaStgSyn::LookupLit
arms).

Today those stale indices usually fall outside the runtime SourceMap and
resolve to nothing — errors/115_render_as_invalid_format and
errors/142_render_unknown_format carry error smid=3055 and print no primary
label. But user-file Smids are minted in the SAME u32 space starting from 1,
so a large enough user file makes the stale index VALID and the diagnostic
points confidently at an unrelated line.

Reproduced on master and on the eu-1tkk.7.21 branch, blob mode, release build:

  # 800 pad declarations, then:
  result: "hello" render-as(:badformat)

  error: unknown render format 'badformat'
    help: supported formats for render-as are: :yaml, :json, :toml, :text, :edn, :html
    ┌─ big.eu:1:9
    │
  1 │ pad1: 1 + 1
    │         ^

A wrong location is worse than no location. This is NOT the eu-1tkk.7.21
root cause (that was the Smid::global_slot stamp overwriting call sites) and
is not fixed by it.

Fix is not a blanket elision: reconstruct_form / reconstruct are also used by
the prelude_slot_override path (set_prelude_slot_override flattens a
freshly-compiled LambdaForm whose Smids ARE valid against the live
SourceMap), so the elision needs an explicit blob-baked discriminator.

Overlaps the resolve_trace_entry work in PRs #1079 and #1084 — sequence
accordingly.
close_reason: Fixed: a 900-declaration render-as(:badformat) repro shows no wrong label; StgArena::rebase_baked_smid (eu-7x0r, 0.14)

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
STILL OPEN after eu-1tkk.7.32. Much better evidence available now.

Established empirically (not assumed) that the annotation save/restore does NOT
make neutralisation moot - the opposite. New sweep: 8 prelude-routed error
shapes in a 900-declaration file, checking whether the primary label names an
unrelated padNNN declaration. Both engines, blob mode:

  master                              8 of 8 WRONG
  lifecycle fix, neutralisation OFF   4 of 8 WRONG
  lifecycle fix, neutralisation ON    2 of 8 WRONG

So the two mechanisms are complementary and BOTH are required; disabling
neutralisation regressed bit.and and //= back to blaming pads.

RESIDUAL, still wrong on both engines, and equally wrong on master (so
pre-existing, not caused by eu-1tkk.7.32):

  result: "nope" parse-as(:notaformat)   -> blames pad758
  result: {a: 1} lookup(:missing)        -> blames pad282

EU_ERROR_TRACE_DUMP on the lookup case:
  error smid: smid=1160 file=3 span=4746..4747 ann="pad282"
  env_trace  [0] smid=1160 ... ann="pad282"
  stack_trace[0] smid=1160 ... ann="pad282"
  stack_trace[1] smid=3638 ... ann="result"   <- the correct answer, present

Note the Smid is NOT a stale xtask index: SourceMap resolves it to a genuine
entry minted while desugaring the user's own pad282 declaration, annotated
"pad282". So this residue is a live-Smid leak of the eu-og3u6 class, not the
baked-Smid aliasing eu-1tkk.7.29 was originally filed for - the two symptoms
look identical from the outside. to_diagnostic then uses the error's own Smid
because it is a user file, never consulting the stack trace that holds the
right answer.

Two candidate fixes, both need measuring against the 716-run corpus:
  (a) find and close the remaining leak path (something still carries pad282
      into the erroring closure's environment and live annotation)
  (b) have to_diagnostic prefer a user frame from the stack trace over its own
      Smid when the two disagree - narrower, but treats the symptom

Reproducer: scratchpad/eu-1tkk-7-29-sweep2.sh <binary> <root> <label>.

comments.text: Fixed: a 900-declaration render-as(:badformat) repro shows no wrong label; StgArena::rebase_baked_smid (eu-7x0r, 0.14) (owner grooming, 17 Nov; staleness check on master d1b867d). Owner: "go".

title: Audit every CI gate and test-infrastructure assertion for whether it can actually fail
description:
Five distinct dead or hollow gates were found in a single week (2026-07-20..27), all by accident while fixing something else. The common factor is not carelessness in any one change: it is that this project has several mechanisms by which a gate can look green while asserting nothing, and we have no systematic check for them.

The five found so far:
1. eu-7x0r / eu-5yn9v — blob-mode CI coverage was an ALLOWLIST (eu test on the .eu harness plus two named tests). All 174 error .expect fixtures ran source-prelude only.
2. eu-5yn9v — prelude_blob_ok is a build.rs cfg, so a '#![cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]' test file compiles to ZERO tests without a blob. Absent coverage is indistinguishable from passing coverage.
3. eu-3skeg — build.rs needed an explicit rerun-if-changed for src/eval/intrinsics.rs; emitting ANY such directive opts cargo out of whole-package tracking, so the gate would have been silently dead.
4. eu-ziq8o — error .expect sidecars assert message TEXT but never source location. 083_array_arith_mismatch named the wrong declaration in every shipped release with a green test throughout.
5. eu-vbctt — test_config_matrix_blob_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal never exercises the blob-core path: it runs eu check, which always loads prelude source. Proven by injecting a fault that left it green while an eval-path equivalent went red.

Plus two near-misses inside individual fixes, where a fix's own new test would have PASSED without the fix: the eu-pazes complexity gate (ran in blob mode, where the old definition is linear) and the eu-r4647 safeguard (planted its Smid on an App node that synthesise_app never reads, so the warning carried Smid(None)).

TASK: enumerate the ways a gate here can silently not gate, then audit against that list rather than fixing instances as they surface. Candidate mechanisms to check for:
- cfg-gated test files that can compile to zero tests
- path-filtered workflows (.github/workflows/tree-sitter.yaml only triggers on certain paths, so job counts differ legitimately between PRs — but a genuinely required check could be filtered out unnoticed)
- allowlisted test selections inside CI jobs rather than whole-suite runs
- assertions matching on the wrong output channel (a regex that matches the 'stack trace:' note rather than the primary label line)
- tests whose fixtures are too small for the defect class (Smid/SourceMap/allocation-group bugs need LARGE fixtures)
- tests calling an entry point that is not the one users hit
- build-script staleness (a change that only takes effect at build time, with no dependency declared)

ACCEPTANCE: a written inventory of gate mechanisms and their failure modes; a pass over the existing suite against it; a bead per instance found; and where cheap, a meta-check that fails loudly (e.g. a test file contributing zero tests should be an error, not silence).

Owner context: 0.14 is the diagnostics release and the gate is 'diagnostics improvement PROVEN'. A proof mechanism that cannot fail proves nothing.
notes:
== INVENTORY OF GATE FAILURE MECHANISMS (clarion, 2026-07-27) ==

Measured on master a1af1f0b in a worktree, both prelude modes and both
engines. Blob generated locally; `prelude_blob_ok` confirmed from the
build-script output (target/debug/build/eucalypt-*/output), never inferred
from the blob file existing.

BASELINE: exactly three pre-existing blob-mode failures, all eu-7x0r ---
diagnostics_invariants::secondary_labels_do_not_excerpt_library_internals,
diagnostics_invariants::debug_trace_restores_the_uncurated_trace, and
harness_test::test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace. Nothing else.

--- M1. A cfg-gated compilation unit contributes zero tests, reports green.
DETECT: `cargo test --test X -- --list | grep -c ': test'` per target per
config.
MEASURED blob-less: diagnostics_blame_plumbing_test = 0 tests, exit 0. Every
other target non-zero (harness_test 506, lsp_test 111, io_args_test 12,
property_test 11, bytecode_io_differential_test 7, diagnostics_invariants 3,
diagnostics_json_emission 3, fuzz_regression_test 3, git_import_test 2,
conform_test 1, diagnostics_metadata_span_test 1, tick_parity_test 1). Grows
to three gated files as #1074 (ef1 deprecation gate) and #1085
(diagnostics_snapshots' two #[cfg(prelude_blob_ok)] tests) land.
CATCHES: a dropped/renamed `cargo xtask prelude-compile` step making a whole
job vacuous rather than red.
META-CHECK: DONE in PR #1095 (tests/gate_liveness.rs) --- a registry of every
conditionally compiled test file plus a STATIC check that each blob-gated
file's named CI job exists and runs prelude-compile, plus
EU_REQUIRE_PRELUDE_BLOB=1. Also DONE in PR #1094
(scripts/diagnostics-gate.sh fails when a target reports "0 passed").

--- M2. Path-filtered workflow.
Only .github/workflows/tree-sitter.yaml. Filter omits src/syntax outside
rowan/ and any new corpus directory; a genuinely required check could vanish
from the rollup and look normal, because job counts legitimately differ
between PRs.
PROPOSED (approved, NOT DONE): drop the path filter --- the job is short and
the filter buys nothing against the risk.

--- M3. Allowlisted test selection inside a CI job; a filter matching nothing
exits 0.
PROVEN: `cargo test --test diagnostics_invariants no_such_test -- --exact`
-> "test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 3 filtered out", exit 0.
INSTANCES: diagnostics-blob-mode job (2 selections); wasm job
(`cargo test --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib wasm_tests`).
The comment "Widen the cargo test invocations below as each lands" had
nothing enforcing it.
FIX: DONE in PR #1094 --- scripts/diagnostics-gate.sh runs whole targets with
--skip and then requires each skipped test to STILL FAIL, so a fix turns the
job red until its line is deleted. wasm job NOT addressed.

--- M4. Assertion on the wrong channel, or a substring a note also satisfies.
172 of 174 error .expect sidecars assert message text only; 2 pin a
file:line:col. A pattern like "nth" is satisfied by the `stack trace:` note
even when the primary label is wrong --- 083_array_arith_mismatch shipped a
wrong location for releases with a green test (eu-ziq8o).
NEW INSTANCE FOUND: five error fixtures have NO sidecar
(008_op_spacing.eu, x007_bad_block_element.eu, x018_missing_comma.eu,
x021_dot_in_key.eu, x022_redef.eu). Only 008 has a generated test
(test_error_008 at harness_test.rs:1086); per `tester::error_test`'s own
doc, "If no .expect sidecar exists, the test is treated as unvalidated and
passes without running". That test does not execute its fixture at all and
cannot fail.
PROPOSED (approved, NOT DONE): give all five a sidecar, and make the tester
REJECT a sidecar-less error fixture rather than passing it --- the
silent-pass behaviour is the defect, the five instances are symptoms.

--- M5. Fixture too small for the defect class.
The invariant gate corpus --- the flagship "diagnostics PROVEN" gate --- is 9
fixtures, 21 lines TOTAL, max 4 lines, with region_start_line..region_end_line
spans of 1-2 lines inside 2-4 line files. Invariant (iii) is near-vacuous at
that size. Both headline defects of 0.14 are invisible in it BY
CONSTRUCTION: eu-og3u6 (anchor on the wrong declaration) needs >= 2 user
declarations; eu-7x0r / eu-r4647 (Smid aliasing) need a user SourceMap that
grows past the blob's ~7357 baked Smids. #1085 adds large fixtures but only
to the SNAPSHOT corpus, not this one.
PROPOSED (approved, NOT DONE): add fixtures large enough to catch both
classes, and reject a region spanning the whole file.

--- M6. Test calls an entry point users do not hit.
eu-vbctt confirmed (see that bead). LARGER INSTANCE, filed separately: the
~500 non-error harness tests run IN-PROCESS --- harness_test.rs:55
`tester::test(opt)` -> `tester::run_plans` -> `InProcessTester` ->
`driver::eval` --- bypassing src/bin/eu.rs, which is where the blob-core
type-check dispatch (`run_type_checker_from_blob_core`) and the type-warning
emission live. Only the error tests (`error_test_with_binary`) and the
typecheck tests spawn the binary.

--- M7. Build-script staleness / undeclared inputs.
build.rs emits 6 explicit rerun-if-changed, which opts out of whole-package
change tracking (eu-3skeg). NEW INSTANCE: BYTECODE_WIRE_FORMAT_VERSION = 5 is
declared TWICE --- build.rs:38 and xtask/src/main.rs:57 --- kept in step by
"MUST match" comments and nothing else. Divergence gives a permanent hash
mismatch -> prelude_blob_stale -> the blob path silently falls back to source
AND every cfg(prelude_blob_ok) test compiles to zero.
STATUS: already addressed by PR #1082 (moves the constant, the hash recipe,
the input paths and the staleness verdict into src/eval/stg/wire_format.rs
which build.rs include!s and xtask imports, and adds the missing
rerun-if-changed for the intrinsic catalogue). NOT duplicated here.
Also worth recording in build.rs: restoring a blob with `mv`/`cp -p`
preserves mtime, so cargo does not rerun build.rs and the stale cfg persists.

--- M8. (NEW) A skip that returns success.
`skip_on_windows` in #1085's tests/diagnostics_snapshots.rs (eu-1tkk.7.22) ---
an early `return` from the test body, i.e. green. Also
`tester::run_plans` (src/driver/tester.rs:173) silently skips a `requires-io`
plan when --allow-io is absent and continues with exit 0. Dormant today
(harness_test's io_opts grants it) but a new IO test added with plain
`opts()` would skip forever.
PROPOSED: skips should be counted and asserted against an expected count, or
expressed as #[ignore] so the runner reports them.

--- M9. (NEW) A relaxation that makes an assertion arm unreachable.
`assert!(heapsyn || unexpected_pass.is_empty())` in
corpus_satisfies_invariants. Separately, NO corpus fixture is marked
xfail today, so unexpected_pass is always empty and the arm was vacuous on
BOTH engines. The (iv) invariant's own comment in violations() is the model
for how to avoid this.
FIX: DONE in PR #1094 --- per-engine xfail_engines markers, the blanket
relaxation deleted, and the verdict extracted as a pure function with a unit
test per arm so the ratchet branch is provably reachable whatever the corpus
contains.

--- M10. (NEW) A duplicated constant kept in step by a comment.
eu-0cc1's TRACE_BUDGET (FIXED in PR #1094 by importing the crate constant);
M7's BYTECODE_WIRE_FORMAT_VERSION (PR #1082).
DETECT: grep for "MUST match", "shared with", "cannot drift apart".

--- M11. (NEW) Whole-suite coverage asymmetry between configurations.
The ONLY full `cargo test` in CI is the "Test Suite" job, which is
deliberately blob-less. Every blob-mode job runs `eu test tests/harness`,
which does NOT include tests/harness/errors/** --- those are generated Rust
tests in harness_test.rs. So all 174 error fixtures, the corpus that is
supposed to gate 0.14 diagnostics, run source-prelude ONLY. Proven:
test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace fails under a blob and no CI job can see
it. This is eu-5yn9v ("invert the default"), P1.

== STATUS ==
DONE (PRs open, not merged):
  #1094 fix/clarion-diagnostics-gate-infrastructure --- M3, M9, M10
        (TRACE_BUDGET), plus M1's per-target zero-test check; eu-1tkk.7.17,
        eu-0cc1.
  #1095 fix/clarion-gate-liveness --- M1 registry + static supplier check.
APPROVED BUT NOT STARTED: M2 (drop tree-sitter path filter), M4 (sidecars +
reject sidecar-less error fixtures), M5 (large invariant-corpus fixtures +
region validation).
FILED SEPARATELY: M6.
NOT MINE: M11/eu-5yn9v; M7 (PR #1082).

Every gate touched in #1094 and #1095 was fault-injection verified per site,
rebuilt each time --- 12 injections in total, listed in the two PR bodies.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: In 0.16.0 (owner grooming, 17 Nov; staleness check on master d1b867d), re-scoped: M1/M3/M7/M9/M10 are done; M11 is eu-5yn9v. Remaining: M2 (tree-sitter.yaml path filter for Cargo files) and M4 (five fixtures without sidecars, including 008_op_spacing, that the tester passes unvalidated).

title: error harness .expect sidecars assert message text but never source location
description:
Found while fixing eu-og3u6 (clarion, 2026-07-27).

Every error harness fixture under tests/harness/errors/ is gated by a
single stderr regex in its .expect sidecar. Almost all of them assert
only the message text (often just the fixture filename). None of the
nine fixtures whose diagnostics eu-og3u6 changed asserted the primary
label's file:line:col.

Consequence: a wrong-location regression is invisible to the harness.
083_array_arith_mismatch has been naming the wrong declaration in its
stack-trace note ('a', line 2, instead of 'c', line 4 — the declaration
that actually called arr.add) in every release that shipped it, with a
green test the whole time. eu-og3u6 itself survived because 193, the
one fixture that does assert a location, is a two-declaration file in
which the bug is invisible by construction.

0.14 is the diagnostics release; the corpus that is supposed to gate
diagnostics quality currently gates only message wording.

Proposal:
- require every error .expect regex to pin the primary label's own
  file:line:col, ahead of the 'stack trace:' marker so that a note-only
  match cannot satisfy it (194_og3u6_trace_anchor.eu.expect is the
  pattern to copy);
- audit the existing ~179 sidecars and add the assertion where the
  location is a meaningful property of the fixture;
- consider having the tester reject an error .expect whose regex
  contains no location, so the gap cannot reappear silently.

Related: eu-ntwg.2 (tester improvements).
notes:
DESIGN CONSTRAINT discovered the hard way (clarion, PR #1090, 2026-07-27). You CANNOT pin blob-only locations in .expect sidecars.

A .expect sidecar has NO NOTION OF PRELUDE MODE. The deliberately blob-less 'Test Suite' CI job runs the same fixtures, so a sidecar asserting a location that only exists under a blob fails that job. An agent tried exactly this and CI caught it - three fixtures red.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: 'require every error .expect regex to pin the primary label's file:line:col' cannot be applied uniformly. Locations that differ between blob and source mode, or exist in only one, must be asserted somewhere prelude-mode-aware. The working pattern is tests/diagnostics_blame_plumbing_test.rs - '#[cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]', run by the blob-mode job, reading the primary-label line via primary_label_position. Note the cfg-gated-file hazard: without a blob such a file compiles to ZERO tests and reports green, so the inventory must also fail loudly when a gated file contributes nothing.

So this bead needs a THREE-WAY split, not one rule: (a) locations identical in both modes -> pin in the .expect sidecar; (b) locations that differ or are blob-only -> assert in a prelude-mode-aware Rust test; (c) the 13-down-to-4 divergence inventory in tests/diagnostics/DIVERGENCE.md is the list of (b) cases.

ANCHOR PATTERN, verified: '┌─[^\n]*<fixture>\.eu:LINE:COL'. The [^\n]* cannot cross a line, and stripping the ┌─ line - leaving the location only in the 'stack trace:' note - was directly verified to give no match. Adopt this corpus-wide; matching the note instead of the label is a mistake made twice this week.

RELATED GATE WEAKNESS, same class as this bead: an .expect that pins a location can still be satisfied by to_diagnostic's TRACE FALLBACK rather than by the annotation plumbing under test. Demonstrated on 171_yaml_large_uint - replacing machine.annotation() with Smid::default() left the output byte-identical. So pinning a location gates that a correct label is PRESENT, not that the mechanism producing it works. Where the plumbing itself matters, it needs its own test.

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
From eu-1tkk.7.20 (furnace, PR #1089) — a fault-injection result eu-ziq8o should build in.

TIGHTENING A SIDECAR TO ASSERT THE LOCATION IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN.
The location assertion can pass for the wrong reason.

171_yaml_large_uint.eu.expect now asserts the primary label's file:line:col
anchored on the label line:

    ┌─[^\n]*171_yaml_large_uint\.eu:4:7

Verified the anchoring works: stripping the '┌─' line from the real stderr,
leaving the same location present only in the 'stack trace:' note, gives NO
match. So a note-only match cannot satisfy it — the property eu-ziq8o wants.

BUT it still does not gate the plumbing that produces the location. Fault
injection replacing machine.annotation() with Smid::default() at the error
construction site left the output BYTE-IDENTICAL and the test PASSED,
because ExecutionError::to_diagnostic falls back to searching env_trace then
stack_trace and recovered the same location from there.

So the assertion gates 'a correct primary label is present', not 'the error
carries the right Smid'. Where those two agree, a Smid regression is
invisible even to a location-asserting sidecar.

IMPLICATION FOR THE AUDIT: when adding a location assertion to a sidecar,
verify it can fail for the reason intended — break the Smid at the
construction site, not just the message — and record whether it gated. Where
the trace fallback masks it, either say so on the fixture or pick a fixture
whose error Smid and trace Smid differ.

The '┌─[^\n]*file\.eu:L:C' anchor plus the strip-the-label-line check is
offered as the corpus-wide pattern; the caveat above is the part a
mechanical sweep would otherwise miss.

title: [test][diagnostics] test_config_matrix_blob_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal does not exercise the blob-core path at all — eu check never uses it
description:
Found by clarion while fixing eu-r4647.

`tests/harness_test.rs::test_config_matrix_blob_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal`
claims to compare "the blob-core merged check (default config)" against
"the source-prelude merged check (EU_SOURCE_PRELUDE=1)". It does not.

It invokes `eu check --strict <file>`. `eu check` goes through
`driver::check::check()` -> `run_type_checker()`, which unconditionally
`loader.load()`s every input including the prelude resource, from source.
It never touches a `PreludeBlob` and never calls
`run_type_checker_from_blob_core`. That function has exactly one
non-test caller: `src/bin/eu.rs`, on the EVAL path.

So both arms of the "matrix" take the identical source-prelude code path,
and `EU_SOURCE_PRELUDE=1` changes nothing about what is compared. The test
is a tautology: it cannot fail for any blob-vs-source divergence, which is
the entire property it exists to assert (eu-rb5n condition 2/4).

CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY: an asymmetric fault injected into
`SourceMap::info_at` (a bug that only manifests when a foreign Smid range
has been reserved, i.e. only on the blob-core path) left this test GREEN,
while the same injection turned an eval-path equivalent RED. See
`test_blob_core_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal_on_a_large_file`, added by
the eu-r4647 PR, which drives `eu --strict <file>` (no subcommand) instead
and does discriminate.

WANTED: either repoint the existing matrix at the eval path, or keep it as
a source-path regression test and rename/redocument it so it stops
claiming coverage it does not have. Note that repointing may surface real
divergences that have been invisible until now — that is the point, but it
should be expected rather than treated as a new regression.

Related: this is the third instance this week of a test whose stated
rationale does not match what it exercises (see eu-r4647 for the other
two, both in the same area).
notes:
CLARION 2026-07-27 --- investigated, NOT yet fixed. No code written for this
bead; the branch fix/clarion-eu-vbctt-blob-core-path was created and deleted
unused.

CONFIRMED, and the fix is viable. src/bin/eu.rs:183-213 is the only
non-test caller of run_type_checker_from_blob_core, and it is on the EVAL
path; `eu check` goes through driver::check::check() -> run_type_checker(),
which always loads prelude source. Repointing the matrix at
`eu --strict <file>` (no subcommand) does reach the blob-core path, and I
verified all three existing fixtures behave: 065, 104 and 111 each give exit
1 with BYTE-IDENTICAL stderr and stdout between the default (blob) arm and
EU_SOURCE_PRELUDE=1. So repointing surfaces no pre-existing divergence.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT for whoever picks this up. Repointed and left ungated, the
test is STILL vacuous in the blob-less 'Test Suite' job (both arms take the
source path) --- and that is the only CI job that runs `cargo test` as a
whole. So the fix needs a blob-mode home. Three routes:
  (a) put the test in tests/diagnostics_blame_plumbing_test.rs, which is
      already #![cfg(prelude_blob_ok)], already registered in PR #1095's
      REGISTRY, and already run by the diagnostics-blob-mode job via PR
      #1094's scripts/diagnostics-gate.sh --- ZERO new registry entries, zero
      new CI invocations, zero conflicts. This is the cheapest correct route
      and the one I had settled on;
  (b) a new cfg-gated target, which needs a REGISTRY entry (#1095) and a new
      CI invocation (#1094) --- both mine, both unmerged, so it stacks;
  (c) eu-5yn9v's inversion, which subsumes the problem.
Per the bead's own second option, the existing harness_test.rs test should
ALSO be renamed/redocumented so it stops claiming blob-core coverage it does
not have.

NOTE THAT PR #1084 ALREADY ADDS an eval-path equivalent,
test_blob_core_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal_on_a_large_file, in
harness_test.rs under #[cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]. No CI job runs harness_test
with a blob (eu-5yn9v), so that test currently has a home in no job at all
and is not registered by #1095 --- it will need one of the routes above too.

STALE CLAIM CONFIRMED AND REMOVED. The comment in
.github/workflows/build-rust.yaml asserting that harness-level typecheck
tests 010/011/013/063/085 are 'actively red under blob mode (eu-rqwh, in
progress)' is FALSE. eu-rqwh closed on 2026-07-24. I ran the full
`cargo test --test harness_test` with a verified blob
(cargo:rustc-cfg=prelude_blob_ok read from the build-script output): all five
pass, and the only failure in 506 tests was test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace,
itself eu-7x0r. PR #1094 deletes the claim.

Baseline for anyone verifying: exactly three pre-existing blob-mode failures
on master a1af1f0b, all eu-7x0r ---
diagnostics_invariants::secondary_labels_do_not_excerpt_library_internals,
diagnostics_invariants::debug_trace_restores_the_uncurated_trace, and
harness_test::test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace.

title: [P1][ci] blob mode is the SHIPPED path but CI validates it by allowlist - invert the default
description:
REMAINING SCOPE (re-scoped 2026-08-03, post-0.14 housekeeping eu-bg55t): invert the PRIMARY cargo test configuration. The 'Test Suite' job in .github/workflows/build-rust.yaml (now explicitly named 'Test Suite (source-prelude fallback, no blob)') still runs the full cargo test suite blob-less, so blob mode — the shipped path — is validated by the dedicated 'Blob-mode cargo tests (all mode-sensitive targets)' job but is still not the PRIMARY cargo test configuration. Wanted: make blob mode the default configuration for the primary cargo test job, while KEEPING a deliberate, broad source-prelude job — furnace's 2026-07-27 measurement (comments below) shows a prelude-inlining defect class (e.g. eu-gua64, 2^N vs linear) is structurally observable ONLY in source mode, so the source job must run the harness suite, not a token invocation, and must fail loudly if it silently narrows.

HISTORY (original scope, filed 2026-07-26 under the owner directive 'this must end now, blob mode is the primary use case'): blob-mode CI coverage was an ALLOWLIST — the whole cargo test suite (all 174 error .expect fixtures, typecheck fixtures, unit tests) ran source-prelude only; cfg(prelude_blob_ok) files silently compiled to zero tests; the diagnostics-blob-mode job was scoped by --exact to exclude the known-red tests; and a stale workflow comment asserted phantom red typecheck tests. Four hiding mechanisms documented in the comments. DELIVERED since: eu-7x0r fixed (PR #1079, whole suite green under blob on both engines); scripts/blob-mode-tests.sh derives the mode-sensitive target list FROM THE TREE (17 targets, up from 4) with an EMPTY ratchet exclusion list; tests/gate_liveness.rs fails if discovery and registry drift, and requires the supplier job to RUN each target; EU_REQUIRE_PRELUDE_BLOB=1 makes a silently-ineffective blob a red job; job names state their mode (PR #1108, eu-1tkk.7.43, shipped in 0.14.0). Items (2) and (3) of the original WANTED list are done; item (1) — the primary-job inversion — is this bead's remaining scope.
notes:
FOURTH HIDING MECHANISM + A STALE BLOCKER, both verified by the coordinator against .github/workflows/build-rust.yaml lines 172-190 (2026-07-27).

MECHANISM 4 - the trap for an auditor. The 'Diagnostics blob-mode integration' job DOES generate a blob and DOES invoke diagnostics_invariants - but scopes it to 'cargo test --test diagnostics_invariants corpus_satisfies_invariants -- --exact', excluding the two eu-7x0r tests by omission. The job comment names both tests and says 'Widen the cargo test invocations below as each lands' - and NOTHING ENFORCES THAT WIDENING. So the one job that looks purpose-built to catch this class is deliberately scoped not to. An auditor sees a green job called 'Diagnostics blob-mode integration' and concludes the area is covered. Widening it must be an explicit, tracked step of the inversion, not left to a comment.

Mechanisms 1 and 2 COMPOSE rather than overlap, confirmed concretely: test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace is tests/harness/errors/193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace.eu with a .eu.expect sidecar, driven only through run_error_test -> tester::error_test_with_binary under 'cargo test' - and 'cargo test' never runs under a blob.

STALE BLOCKER - GOOD NEWS, THE INVERSION IS LESS BLOCKED THAN THE COMMENT SAYS. The same comment claims 'harness-level typecheck tests 010/011/013/063/085 are actively red under blob mode (eu-rqwh, in progress)'. eu-rqwh was CLOSED on 2026-07-24, fixed and merged in PR #1059 (master f242bbc5). Wicket's verification on that PR explicitly confirmed all five typecheck tests pass BOTH with and without a blob, and recorded an 8 -> 3 master failure delta with the remaining three tracked as eu-7x0r. A blob-mode 'cargo test --no-fail-fast' on a1af1f0b independently shows test_193 as the only HARNESS failure.

CONSEQUENCE: the comment lists two blockers; only one is real. Once #1079 lands there is nothing left blocking the widening. Update or delete that comment as part of this bead - a stale CI comment asserting phantom red tests is itself a reason someone will decline to widen.
CLARION 2026-07-27, from the eu-oxtcq audit (mechanism M11). Two things
confirmed on master a1af1f0b that bear on this bead:

1. THE 010/011/013/063/085 CLAIM IS STALE. The comment in
   .github/workflows/build-rust.yaml asserting those harness-level typecheck
   fixtures are 'actively red under blob mode (eu-rqwh, in progress)' is
   false. eu-rqwh closed on 2026-07-24. Full `cargo test --test harness_test`
   with a verified blob (cargo:rustc-cfg=prelude_blob_ok read from the
   build-script output, not inferred from the file existing): all five pass.
   The ONLY failure in 506 tests was test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace, itself
   eu-7x0r. PR #1094 deletes the stale claim.

2. THE SCALE OF WHAT IS UNCOVERED IS MEASURABLE. The only full `cargo test`
   in CI is the 'Test Suite' job, deliberately blob-less. Every blob-mode job
   runs `eu test tests/harness`, which does NOT include
   tests/harness/errors/** --- those are generated Rust tests in
   harness_test.rs. So all 174 error .expect fixtures run source-prelude
   only, and test_193's blob-mode failure is invisible to every job.

Two pieces of machinery now exist to build the inversion on, both in open
unmerged PRs: scripts/diagnostics-gate.sh (PR #1094) runs a WHOLE target with
a ratcheted exclusion list and fails when a target reports '0 passed'; and
tests/gate_liveness.rs (PR #1095) statically asserts that each blob-gated
file's named CI job exists and runs prelude-compile. Inverting the default
for harness_test should reuse the former rather than adding another
allowlist.

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED, AND IT CAN WIDEN ALL THE WAY (clarion, 2026-07-26, PR #1079 fixing eu-7x0r):
- The ENTIRE cargo test suite passes under a blob on BOTH engines. Measured: blob+bytecode 2134/0, blob+heapsyn 2134/0, blobless+bytecode 2124/0, blobless+heapsyn 2124/0.
- The whole diagnostics_invariants file passes under a blob (all 3 tests) - the allowlist can be removed ENTIRELY, not merely widened.
- All 506 harness tests pass under a blob, INCLUDING all 172 error tests with .expect sidecars (the diagnostics-quality surface this bead was filed about).
- Nothing else is red. So items (1) invert the default and (3) remove the allowlist need no further exclusions.

CONCRETE TRAP FOR ITEM (2) - make the loud-fail-on-zero-tests check robust to this: restoring lib/prelude.blob with an OLDER mtime than the last build does NOT retrigger build.rs, so cfg(prelude_blob_ok) stays OFF and '#![cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]' files silently compile to ZERO tests while the board looks green. 'touch build.rs' forces re-evaluation. This is precisely the 'absent coverage is indistinguishable from passing coverage' mode - a naive zero-test check that itself depends on mtime ordering would inherit the same blind spot.

SEQUENCING: gated on PR #1079 landing (it carries the eu-7x0r fix). Do not widen before then.

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
FURTHER EVIDENCE FOR THIS BEAD (wicket, reviewing PR #1080): the new error test tests/harness/errors/194_8a49h_library_blame.eu is gated ONLY in source-prelude mode. The 'Bytecode + blob harness' job runs './target/release/eu test --allow-io tests/harness', which does NOT validate .expect sidecars under tests/harness/errors/, and the plain 'Test Suite' job is deliberately blob-less.

That is notable because the SV3 manifestation of the very bug this test guards was FOUND IN BLOB MODE. A regression test for a bug discovered on the shipped path currently cannot run on the shipped path. (The defect does reproduce in source mode too, so the test gates where it runs - but the asymmetry is exactly what this bead exists to remove.)

Wicket verified the test passes in blob mode locally, so widening will not red it.

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
THE BLIND SPOT RUNS BOTH WAYS — keep a source-prelude job when inverting
(furnace, 2026-07-27, measured on master a1af1f0b while settling eu-pazes).

This bead documents blob-mode coverage that is absent. There is a symmetric
gap in the other direction, and inverting the default without care will
create it: BLOB MODE CANNOT GATE A PRELUDE-INLINING DEFECT AT ALL.

WHY. In blob mode the prelude arrives as already-compiled baked globals, so
the core inliner never sees prelude bodies and never beta-reduces them. On
the source path the prelude is compiled with the user's unit and IS inlined.
Any defect whose mechanism is "inlining a prelude combinator" is therefore
invisible to every blob-mode job, by construction — not flaky, not
under-covered, structurally unobservable.

MEASURED, same release binary, master a1af1f0b, superseded max-of,
`range(1, N) max-of`, timeout+heap-limit wrapped:

  config              N=16   N=20   N=22    N=1000  N=5000  N=20000
  source, ascending   124ms  699ms  2568ms  >90s    >90s    >90s
  blob,   ascending    44ms   41ms    43ms    47ms    72ms    153ms

Same binary, same expression, same input. Source mode is 2^N; blob mode is
linear and looks perfectly healthy at every size. The defect is real
(eu-gua64: `beta_reduce`, src/core/inline/reduce.rs:242, substitutes
arguments with no occurrence count, so a callee using a parameter twice —
`max(l, r): if(l > r, l, r)` — copies its caller's recursive call and gives
T(n) = 2·T(n-1)).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S ITEM (1). The single retained source-prelude job
is not a legacy courtesy or a fallback smoke test — it is the ONLY place this
class of defect can be caught. Please keep it, and keep it broad enough to
run the harness suite rather than a token invocation. "Invert the default"
must not become "delete source-mode coverage".

CONSEQUENCE FOR ITEM (2). The same reasoning applies to the loud-failure
requirement: a source-prelude job that silently narrows to a handful of tests
is the same failure mode as `#![cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]` compiling to zero
tests — absent coverage indistinguishable from passing coverage, just with
the polarity flipped.

WORKED EXAMPLE ALREADY IN TREE. `test_195_pazes_max_of_linear`
(tests/harness_test.rs, PR #1075) passes `--source-prelude` deliberately and
documents why: without the flag the test cannot fail even with the defective
definition restored, because blob mode measures it linear. That test is the
concrete shape of the coverage this bead must preserve.

Relevant to eu-1tkk.7.4 as well: golden diagnostics snapshots taken only in
the mode that ships will not capture regressions in prelude-inlined core
shape.

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
MECHANISM DETAIL from the eu-frf2o (PR #1087) CI review — three distinct mechanisms hide the blob-mode failures, not one. Whoever inverts the CI default needs all of them named, because fixing only the first leaves two intact.

Concrete specimens throughout: the three failures that are red on master under a blob and green in CI — secondary_labels_do_not_excerpt_library_internals, debug_trace_restores_the_uncurated_trace (both eu-7x0r) and test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace. All three fixed by PR #1079.

1. 'Test Suite' IS BLOB-LESS. Its only test steps are a bare 'cargo test' and 'cargo test --lib' (under EU_GC_STRESS); there is no prelude-compile step anywhere in the job. The workflow states the intent outright: 'the plain "Test Suite" job (deliberately blob-less, to keep the source-prelude fallback exercised)'. So its greenness is evidence about the SOURCE-PRELUDE configuration only. This is the mechanism already captured in the bead description.

2. THE BLOB HARNESS JOBS DO NOT VALIDATE errors/*.expect SIDECARS. 'Bytecode + blob harness' runs './target/release/eu test --allow-io tests/harness', i.e. the in-language .eu assertions only. The 174 error tests under tests/harness/errors/ are validated by their .expect sidecars (exit code + stderr regex) through harness_test.rs's run_error_test -> tester::error_test_with_binary, which only 'cargo test' drives — and 'cargo test' never runs under a blob (mechanism 1). Specimen: test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace is tests/harness/errors/193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace.eu plus a .eu.expect sidecar. Nothing in CI checks that sidecar under a blob.

3. THE BLOB HARNESS JOBS NEVER RUN diagnostics_invariants AT ALL. It is a Rust integration test target (tests/diagnostics_invariants.rs), not a harness .eu file, so 'eu test tests/harness' cannot reach it by construction. That is where both eu-7x0r failures live.

4. (Fourth, and the trap for anyone auditing this quickly.) 'Diagnostics blob-mode integration' DOES generate a blob and DOES invoke diagnostics_invariants — but scopes it to 'cargo test --test diagnostics_invariants corpus_satisfies_invariants -- --exact', excluding the two eu-7x0r tests by omission. The workflow comment names both tests and eu-7x0r explicitly as the reason ('only tests confirmed to PASS under a blob today'). So the one job that looks like it should catch them is deliberately scoped not to. That scoping is correct as a stopgap, but it means widening this job is a required step of the eu-5yn9v inversion, not an optional one — the comment already says 'Widen the cargo test invocations below as each lands', and nothing enforces that.

Same comment also flags harness-level typecheck tests 010/011/013/063/085 as red under blob (eu-rqwh). I did NOT observe those locally on a1af1f0b — my blob run was 506 pass / 1 fail with test_193 the only harness failure — so that note may now be stale. Worth re-checking before it is used as a baseline.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING: I initially inferred from PR #1087's green board that the three failures were a macOS-local artefact. That was wrong, and it is exactly the reasoning this bead exists to kill. My own evidence already disproved it — the same machine ran 507/507 with EU_SOURCE_PRELUDE=1 and red under a blob, so the variable is the blob, not the platform. The inference is easy to make precisely because the board is comprehensive-looking (19 checks, several of them named '... blob harness'). Any fix for this bead should aim at making that inference correct rather than merely discouraged.

comments.author: greg
comments.text: PR #1108 (eu-1tkk.7.43) delivers items (2) and (3) of this bead for the cargo-test surface: scripts/blob-mode-tests.sh runs every prelude-mode-sensitive cargo target (16, up from 4) whole under a blob, discovered from the tree rather than allowlisted, and gate_liveness's supplier check now requires the named job to RUN the target rather than merely build a blob. Item (1) is delivered in substance without inverting the Test Suite job's default: that job stays deliberately blob-less to keep the source-prelude fallback exercised, but is now named 'Test Suite (source-prelude fallback, no blob)' so the mode is legible. All 174 tests/harness/errors fixtures now run in both modes.

comments.author: greg
comments.text: WHY 0.14 RELEASED WITH THIS GATE STILL OPEN (recorded during post-0.14 housekeeping, eu-bg55t, 2026-08-03). The owner's 2026-07-26 release gate was '0.14 will not release until blob-mode CI validation is genuine'. By release day its SUBSTANCE was satisfied: the allowlist was gone (scripts/blob-mode-tests.sh derives all 17 mode-sensitive cargo targets from the tree, empty ratchet exclusion list), tests/gate_liveness.rs makes vanishing coverage a hard failure, EU_REQUIRE_PRELUDE_BLOB=1 makes an ineffective blob a red job, and all 174 error fixtures run under both prelude modes — with the mechanism recorded firing in anger on PR #1104. Blob-mode cargo test validation is therefore genuine. The only part not done was the primary-job inversion: 'Test Suite' remains the blob-less source-fallback job while a dedicated job carries blob-mode cargo tests. That is a job-topology preference, not a coverage gap, so it did not hold the release; this bead is re-scoped to exactly that remaining inversion (keeping a broad source-prelude job, which is the only place prelude-inlining defects such as eu-gua64 are observable).

title: Tree-sitter grammar: juxtaposed definitions with a nested list pattern give ERROR nodes
description: Juxtaposed function definitions whose parameter list pattern contains a nested list pattern parse with the Rowan parser but produce ERROR nodes in the tree-sitter grammar (editors/tree-sitter-eucalypt), failing the 'Corpus parse equivalence' check. Found in PR #1273 (AoC 2025 revision), which had to back those definitions out to the parenthesised form. Fix the grammar and add both shapes as regression cases to the corpus.

title: eu doc omits doc strings on block members

Namespace blocks such as pq / bfs / dijkstra in a library are the motivating case. Expected: eu doc lists nested members with their docs, as it does for top-level bindings.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Raised to P2: owner decision 60 (2026-11-17) prioritises tooling fixes for 0.16.0.

title: Source-compiled prelude: a block-local function with a destructuring list parameter fails with 'infinite loop detected: binding refers to itself'
description: Found in the round-3 confirm review of PR #1258 (issuecomment on fbb14d05). In lib/prelude.eu, index-of's local hit?([i, y]): y = x makes every index-of call that reaches hit? fail with 'error: infinite loop detected: binding refers to itself' when the prelude is compiled from source (no lib/prelude.blob, e.g. the source-prelude, aarch64 sequential and byte-dispatch CI harness jobs). With a blob from cargo xtask prelude-compile the same source gives the right answer. hit?(p): second(p) = x works; hit?([_, y]) and hit?([i, v]) both fail, so the cause is the destructuring parameter. The same destructured local function in a user file works. So the source-prelude compilation path handles a destructuring parameter of a block-local function differently from the blob path. Repro: build without a blob, eu -e 'index-of(2, [1, 2])' on the #1258 head fbb14d0. Needs a regression test that runs on the source-prelude path.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1264 (merged 056681fe): depth-aware substs_depth at the three inline sites in src/core/inline/reduce.rs; unit tests per site, fault-injected.

title: Decision: accept checker false negatives on derived monad combinators to fix id-monad false positive (PR #1261)
description:
PR #1261 (eu-oaz72.170) silences the call-site argument mismatch whenever the parameter is an abstract HKT application (m a, m unresolved) and the argument is not an application. This removes the false positive on id-monad.map(inc, 41) / random.map(inc, random.int(10)), but also removes genuine warnings: under eu check --strict, id-monad.map(inc, "x"), io.map(inc, 41), random.map(inc, 41) and random.join("s") all warned on master and are silent on the PR head 801ed61 (reviewer reproduced). Root cause: m is never instantiated from the binding's monad: metadata.

Options:
A. Merge #1261 as is; file follow-up to resolve m from monad: metadata and restore the warnings (with negative fixtures).

title: Decision: str.matches-with semantics for context-sensitive regexes (PR #1244)
description: PR #1244 implements str.matches-with exactly as the 2026-11-11 note on eu-oaz72.26 fixes it: matches-of(re) map(match-with(re)). That definition re-runs the regex on each matched substring alone, so for regexes whose result depends on surrounding text (^, $, \b, \B, alternation decided by context) the groups differ from the in-context match, and a match can come back as []. Measured: "ax" matches-with("\\Bx") gives [[]]; "aa" matches-with("^(a)|(a)") gives [[a,a,''],[a,a,'']] (in context the second is [a,'',a]); "abc" matches-with("(ab)$|(a)(b)") gives [[ab,ab,'','']] (in context [ab,'',a,b]). Options: (A) keep the composition, document the limitation, test it; (B) a new intrinsic using Regex::captures_iter for one in-context pass (a new intrinsic: owner merges); (C) drop matches-with. PR #1244 stays open pending this decision.
close_reason: Decided: option B (decision 38 on the AoC tracking issue; owner, first-hand, 16 Nov). str.matches-with keeps its name and result but is one in-context pass over the regex's captures in a new intrinsic (MATCHES_WITH). title: GC verify: panic when marking meets an already-forwarded header (a pointer the update phase missed)
description: From eu-oaz72.108 (PR #1196, merged 6d2161c): evacuated blocks are now freed in the same collection, so an old copy is reclaimed at once and a pointer the update phase missed becomes a use-after-free. Add a standing EU_GC_VERIFY check (level 1 or 2, per docs) that panics with a clear diagnostic when mark_object meets an already-forwarded header outside the evacuation window. Both #1196 reviewers' probes found no such pointer; this guards future changes. Validate the full harness under EU_GC_VERIFY=2 + EU_GC_STRESS=1 and POISON; unit test that a deliberately un-updated pointer trips it (fault-injection). GC/memory: two independent rig-reviews.
design:
Invariant used: every scan site marks a heap object before pushing it, and only pushed heap objects are evacuated, so an object forwarded in this collection is always marked with the current mark state. A forwarded header is therefore legitimate only (a) during an evacuating collection's mark phase / post-mark re-traversal, and (b) only when marked. After the update phase no live pointer may reach one.

Checks (src/eval/memory/collect.rs, CollectorHeapView::mark / mark_raw_bytes / mark_array):
1. Mark-in-place collection (mark phase + post-mark re-traversal): any forwarded header -> panic (stale pointer from an earlier evacuation whose old copy is not yet overwritten).
2. Evacuating collection mark phase + post-mark re-traversal: forwarded header that is NOT marked with the current state -> panic (this collection only forwards marked objects).
3. New post-update checkpoint, after the update phase and before release_evacuated_lines frees the old copies: a full traversal from roots with a private visited set (heap marks, line maps, live bytes untouched); any child pointer reaching a forwarded header -> panic naming the pointer, type and forwarding target. This catches the miss in the collection it happens, before #1196's same-collection release turns it into a use-after-free.
Levels: 1 and 2 at EU_GC_VERIFY>=1 (O(1) per mark); 3 at EU_GC_VERIFY>=2 (O(live) + hash set, beside the existing post-update checkpoint). Documented in docs/development/gc-implementation.md and gc_debug.rs.
Cost when unset: each CollectorHeapView carries a per-collection flag computed once; mark()'s existing per-call poison_enabled() gate is replaced by that one flag covering poison + forwarding, so mark() does no more work than before; mark_raw_bytes/mark_array gain one test of a bool field. The check bodies are out of line (#[cold]).
Testability: Heap caches the verify level at construction (as gc_stress), with a cfg(test) setter, so unit tests force the checks without the process-global env var.
Tests: root whose scan_and_update skips a pointer, heap object whose scan_and_update skips its child (both trip check 3); stale root carried into a later mark-in-place collection (check 1) and a later evacuating collection (check 2); clean evacuation with checks forced on passes. Fault injection: disable each check, watch the tests fail.
close_reason: PR #1208 merged (459cb3d): EU_GC_VERIFY>=1 mark-time forwarded-header checks, EU_GC_VERIFY>=2 post-update traversal before release_evacuated_lines; two independent rig-reviews per round; full harness clean under VERIFY=2+STRESS and POISON+VERIFY=2+STRESS; no missed pointer on master.

title: Catenation note precision: wrong location for f(xs nth(0) = 1); note fires when the function comes from the right operand
description: From eu-oaz72.29 (PR #1201): with f(a): a, the error raised for f(xs nth(0) = 1) is located at the call f(...) rather than at the '=' operator whose span carries the catenation marker.
design:
Design (eu-oaz72.133):
1. Left-operand gate (static, at cook). Runtime a2 errors (UnexpectedFunction, CannotReturnFunToCase, NotValue) carry no operand position, and NotCallable at the root op says nothing about which operand was the function, so the gate is decided in shunt.rs when a spine op is recorded. The suggestion '(pipeline head) rest' is a fix only if the step's head is the function. Record a spine op only when (a) the step head is not a literal (number, string, symbol, list or block literal: cannot be the function), and (b) every right operand on the spine up to and including that op is a literal or a plain name (not a call, application, nested operator expression or anaphor, any of which may be a partial application such as nth(0)). So 'xs 1 + nth(0) = 1', 'xs 1 + 2 = 3', 'xs 1 = nth(0)' and 'xs nth(0) + nth(1)' get no note; 'c nth(i) = 2', 'xs nth(0) + k' keep it. Residual: a name bound to a function on the right (xs f + g with g a function) still gets the note; documented.
2. Location: inline/reduce.rs retag_call_site re-stamps the result with the call-site Smid even when the callee body is a bare parameter (f(a): a), so the argument's own application (the = op's span carrying the marker) is lost. Retag only when the callee body itself is an application.
3. Nits: (i) quoted text is rebuilt from lexer tokens, so comments are dropped and whitespace runs collapse; (ii) the NotValue gate uses a shared constant used at the raise site; (iii) atoms carry their Written extent as a pair from cook_soup through split and shunt, removing the parallel-vector invariant.
Fixtures: positive and negative error harness tests plus diagnostics_catenation_note_test cases; fault-injection each gate.
notes: Addendum from #1201 merge review: the note also fires when an operator on the step's leftmost spine gets the function from its RIGHT operand, giving a non-fix suggestion (xs 1 + nth(0) = 1 suggests (xs 1) + nth(0) = 1). Fire only when the function comes from the left operand. Nits: a source comment between atoms is copied into the quoted text; one gate matches the NotValue context string; the atom/extent length invariant is only a debug_assert.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1206 (merged)

Fault-injection verified. Residual: a name bound to a function on the right still gets the note.

title: Exact diagnostic for lone-anaphor scope mistakes (second half of eu-oaz72.29)
description: Split from eu-oaz72.29: PR #1201 delivered the catenation-precedence note; the lone-anaphor half (b) of .29's description is not done. Same rule: the note fires only on the exact trigger; fixtures for the positive and a negative case, fault-injection verified.
design:
Design (implementer, 2026-11-14).
Trigger, all required: (1) cook made an argument of a juxtaposed call f(...) the identity function because the argument's soup is a lone expression anaphor (_ or _N, possibly in parens) that opened its own scope (not subsumed by an enclosing anaphoric scope); (2) a runtime error whose diagnostic's primary label is exactly that call's span (user file); (3) the error says a function arrived where a value was wanted: TypeMismatch found a function, UnexpectedFunction, CannotReturnFunToCase, or NotValue for a function application.
Mechanism (reuses #1201's cook->SourceMap pattern, separate code): cook_soup records the anaphor token Smid of a lone-anaphor lambda in SourceMap; shunt form_apply, on a pseudocall, finds arguments that are such lambdas and records the call keyed by its merged (file, span) with the argument positions and anaphor Smids. ExecutionError::diagnostic_impl looks the primary label up and adds the note. Text read from source, stated as fact, no fix suggested: "note: in 'nth(_)', '_' is the whole argument, so the argument is the identity function: an anaphor's scope ends at the parentheses round it" (multi-argument calls name the argument number). No check-time warning (owner's choice in .29, not taken). Negative fixtures: _ + 1 sections, f(_ + 1, 1), subsumed (_ + f(_)), ordinary function-received errors without a lone anaphor.
close_reason: Merged in PR #1210. A lone-anaphor argument that cook makes the identity function gets a factual note on a function-received error labelled at that call. Fixtures 286/287 and tests/diagnostics_lone_anaphor_note_test.rs, fault-injection verified.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: PR #1210 opened. Positive and negative error fixtures (286/287) plus tests/diagnostics_lone_anaphor_note_test.rs, all fault-injection verified. Note: f(_, 1) is a positive case (cook gives f(λx.x, 1)), not a section. The note cannot fire when the error has no user label ([0,1] map(xs nth(_)), or under -e): that is a separate location gap.

title: = compares numbers through f64, so = and set/dict membership disagree above 2^53
description: From eu-oaz72.10 (PR #1187). num_eq in src/eval/stg/eq.rs converts to f64, so 9007199254740993 = 9007199254740992.0 is true while set/dict membership (ExactNum in src/eval/memory/number.rs) says the values differ. Make = use ExactNum's comparison so the two agree; harness test above 2^53 for =, != and membership.
design: Route both numeric comparison helpers through ExactNum (src/eval/memory/number.rs) so =, != and <,>,<=,>= agree with set/vec/dict key order. num_eq (src/eval/stg/eq.rs): ExactNum::from_number(x) == ExactNum::from_number(y). num_ord (src/eval/stg/arith.rs): same, via cmp. Same small change, so ordering is fixed too: mixed int/float and i64/u64 pairs above 2^53 currently go through f64. 1 = 1.0 and -0.0 = 0.0 stay true (ExactNum compares by value). NaN is unrepresentable in serde_json Number, so the NumericDomainError branch for unordered floats is unreachable; num_ord keeps its Result signature but guards NaN explicitly for safety. Harness test: 9007199254740993 vs 9007199254740992.0 for =, !=, <, >, <=, >= and set membership agreeing with =; 1 = 1.0 retained. Fault injection: revert num_eq/num_ord to f64 and confirm FAIL.

title: c-string: an escaped \{ followed by an interpolation fails to parse
description: From eu-ioz21.2 (PR #1192). c"\{ {n}" fails with 'invalid c-string escape: unexpected end of string in escape'. c"\{lit\}" and c"{n} \}" both work, so the lexer mis-scans an escaped brace when an interpolation follows. Fix in src/syntax/rowan/ with a harness test; check the tree-sitter grammar and TextMate grammar agree.
design: Cause: CStringPatternLexer::next() bumps the first character of a literal run and then calls literal_content(), which handles backslash escapes only for characters it peeks. When that first character is a backslash, the escaped char (here { or }) is peeked as an unescaped brace, so the token ends at the lone backslash and the brace opens an interpolation (escape processing then sees "\" alone: unexpected end of string). Affects c"\{lit}", c"\}" and c"\{ {n}" — any escaped brace at the start of a literal run. Fix: in next(), when the literal token starts with a backslash, bump the escaped character too before literal_content. Tests: lexer unit test plus gating harness test 260_oaz72_114_cstring_escaped_brace.eu. Grammars: tree-sitter (c_escape_sequence token) and TextMate (escape pattern before #interpolation) already handle the input; verified with tree-sitter parse.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1195 (merged): c-string lexer keeps an escaped brace with its backslash; tree-sitter c_string accepts a lone }. Gating test: target test-brace-interpolation in tests/harness/124_cstring_escapes.eu.

title: DECISION: what should integer ^ negative integer return (2 ^ -1)?
description: From eu-oaz72.12 (PR #1190). The 12 Nov decision says integer ^ integer stays an integer (overflow is an error) and is a float only when an operand is a float. It does not cover a negative integer exponent: 2 ^ (0 - 1) returns 0.5 on master and still does after #1190. Options: (1) keep the float 0.5 (exception to the rule, current behaviour); (2) raise an error (integer ^ negative integer is undefined for integers; use 2.0 ^ -1 for a float); (3) integer result by truncation (0), which is surprising. #1190 leaves the behaviour unchanged, so it does not depend on this decision.
close_reason: Owner decision 26 (2026-11-14): integer ^ negative integer keeps returning a float (2 ^ -1 = 0.5), consistent with ÷; never truncate. No code change. Already pinned by tests/harness/080_pow.eu negative-exponent (pow(2, -1) //= 0.5).

title: GC: an evacuated block is freed only at the next collection, so EU_GC_STRESS holds ~2x live under tight limits
description: From eu-oaz72.90 (PR #1185). After evacuation the old copies stay line-marked, so the source block is freed only at the next GC, and the next analysis re-picks it first and wastes the evacuation budget. Consequence: under EU_GC_STRESS, harness 228 now fails at 14-16 MiB heap limits where master passed (CI stress jobs use the default limit and are unaffected). Fix: free evacuated blocks in the same collection, or skip last-evacuated blocks in candidate selection. GC/memory: two independent rig-reviews; gates VERIFY=2, POISON, STRESS, 228 at low limits.
design: Free evacuated space in the same collection. All GC line marking funnels through HeapState::mark_region_in_block(header_ptr, bytes). During an evacuating collection, record each region marked in a candidate block (set by Heap before the mark phase from candidate_block_bases). After the update phase rewrites every pointer, for each candidate block reset its line map and re-mark only the recorded regions whose AllocHeader is not forwarded (objects never queued for evacuation, or whose evacuation failed). The block's line map then shows only data that still lives there: a fully evacuated block is Empty and the lazy sweep files it free (and enforce_footprint_limit can release it) in this cycle, and the next analysis no longer re-picks it. Exact by construction: anything not forwarded keeps its lines. Old copies become reclaimable immediately, so any missed pointer update now shows under EU_GC_POISON=1. Gate: unit test in heap/collect asserting a fully evacuated candidate block has zero marked lines after collect_with_evacuation (and that a retained object's lines stay marked), plus a harness/integration gate running 228 under EU_GC_STRESS at a 14 MiB limit.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1196 (merged): candidate blocks' line maps are redrawn after the update phase without forwarded old copies, so evacuated blocks free in the same collection. 228 passes under EU_GC_STRESS at 10-16 MiB; gc_004 at 10 MiB. Follow-up suggested: standing EU_GC_VERIFY check for reachable forwarded headers.

description: Reviewer follow-ups from PR #1174 (eu-oaz72.58). (1) set.sample / vec.sample hang on a negative count (stream advance; predates #1174): must error like take. (2) A NaN or infinite count fails inside floor rather than with the named non-integer message. (3) Minor: window-all uses two different step-message names; rotate/update-nth check the count twice; __take/__drop carry no blame metadata.
design: Revised after round-1 review (PR #1181). (1) Root cause: private stream-advance stopped only at n = 0, so any negative step count recursed forever (set.sample/vec.sample with n < 0, vec.shuffle of an empty vec). It now stops at n <= 0: a negative sample count behaves like take and random.sample (empty sample, stream unadvanced). No new error case. (2) NaN/±inf cannot reach a count: numbers are serde_json::Number (finite only), and every producing path errors first. No code change; criterion moot. (3) Tidy: window-all's positivity message names 'window-all step'; split-at body moved to private __split-at so rotate/update-nth check once; __take/__drop/__split-at blame: :transparent. Tests: 130_vec.eu negative/zero sample + empty shuffle checks, gated by a 30 s deadline in test_harness_130; 036 split-at/rotate/update-nth checks; fault-injected in both prelude modes.

title: LookupLit: slow path pushes no Update for a Global thunk object; fast path has no gating test
description: Follow-ups from eu-oaz72.87 (PR #1175, merged fce2781). (1) Pre-existing: LookupLit's slow path pushes no Update when the object being looked up is a Global thunk, a possible further loss of sharing. Confirm with a tick-counting repro and fix. (2) The LookupLit fast path has no gating test: no program shape was found that reaches it and lost sharing on master. Find one, or document why the path can't lose sharing.
design: Cause (1): Op::LookupLit's slow path (both dispatch paths) pushed Update only when the object was a Local thunk; for a Global it forced the global's thunk with no blackhole/Update, so the globals slot stayed unevaluated. Reachable only in blob mode, where every prelude binding is a global arity-0 thunk: each user-code set.size / str.len / cal.epoch rebuilds the namespace block (str: ~350 allocs) until something else forces it via enter_global. Repro: range(0,1000) map(f) with f(i): str.len("ab")+i: 453k allocs vs 99k fixed. Fix: obj_slot becomes (frame, index) for Local and Global alike; blackhole + Update target that frame, exactly as enter_global / DirectApp do (eu-fhoo). Source mode is unaffected (prelude bindings are locals there). Gate: allocation budget (rebuilding a namespace costs allocs, ~1 tick), so a harness alloc/tick check in Rust; fails only in blob mode by construction. (2): once the global is updated, later cal.epoch reads take the fast path on a WHNF block with an unevaluated CAF field (epoch: 0 ifields) - candidate fast-path gate; sweeping harness for user-level shapes too.
acceptance_criteria: Repro and fix for (1) with a tick-budget harness check, fault-injection verified in blob and source mode and under EU_PREDECODE=0; (2) gated or documented.
notes: PR #1184. (1) fixed + gated: 236 namespace-lookup, allocation budget (51k fixed vs 405k master, 200k budget), fault-injected per dispatch path; FAILs only in blob mode by construction (source mode never reaches it). (2) documented, not gated: harness sweep with fast-path instrumentation found one hit with an unevaluated field (017, cheap function-valued field of a render-forced block); local .key objects are per-use alias thunks so always take the slow path; only blob-mode namespace globals reach the fast path forced, and their thunk members are cheap CAFs. Comment at the fast path records this.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #1184 (merged): LookupLit slow path now black-holes and updates a Global thunk object (both dispatch paths). Gated by test 236 namespace-lookup (allocation budget), fault-injected per dispatch path; blob-only by construction. Fast path documented (no shape reaches it with a costly unevaluated field).

title: Derived prelude signatures: follow-ups from #1173
description: From the eu-oaz72.77 lane and reviews (PR #1173): (1) propagate signatures through aliases and partial applications; (2) the analysis doesn't see through pipeline steps (head-or derives lazy in its list); (3) errors/110 trace shows one extra boundary frame in blob mode; (4) the signature table is cloned per run; (5) the bench baseline in the report is b8bfb43 (pre-#1169): re-measure against current master.
design:
Design (lane eu-oaz72.92/sig-follow-ups):
(1) analyse_let_rhss computes a signature for every non-lambda binding each round, from that round's derived signatures: bare intrinsic -> its sig; bound var -> the target binding's sig; partial application f(a1..ak) with sig(f) longer than k -> sig(f)[k..]. Resolved in a second pass after the lambdas so a same-group alias never reads a stale signature. derive_top_level_signatures reads the top-level let frames' settled signatures (seeds), so alias and PAP slots (zip-with, zip, ...) get one.
(2) analyse_app flattens an App spine: App(App(g, a), b) is analysed as g applied to a++b for the signature, structure unchanged. head-or derives strict in xs.
(6) SigFrame carries per-binding IF branch positions: __IF -> (1,2); an alias inherits; a lambda whose body is IF over its own params maps them (then -> (0,1)). The branch join uses them, not only a literal __IF.
(7) blob-mode test recomputes the derivation over the source prelude and compares every slot with the embedded blob.
(8) unit tests on hand-built core for alias/PAP/flattened calls (no blob).
(9) blob mode: the user-side analysis takes prelude signatures for Var::Free callees (name_to_slot + blob sigs, by reference).
(4) Executor builds the Arc of slot signatures once in set_prelude_blob.
(3) investigate the 110 extra frame; fix or record won't-fix.
(5) re-measure ticks vs current master, report updated.
acceptance_criteria: Each item fixed with a test, or recorded as won't-fix with a reason; perf numbers under the protocol.
close_reason: PR #1183 merged: items 1,2,4,6,7,8,9 fixed with tests; 3 won't-fix (accurate boundary frame); 5 re-measured in docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-derived-signature-follow-ups.md

title: GC: evacuation never considers unswept or recycled blocks, so a fragmented heap can't be compacted
description: From eu-oaz72.73 (PR #1171). Evacuation analysis only selects among swept candidates, never unswept or recycled blocks, so fragmentation can't be compacted away. Effect: harness 228 fails at --heap-limit-mib 12 (master completes only by holding about 21 MiB); it passes from 16 MiB. GC area: design first, two independent reviews, performance protocol.
design:
Design (before coding), 2026-11-13.

Diagnosis (228 at --heap-limit-mib 12, per-collection log): live ~7 MiB, held ~578 blocks (18 MiB); ~95% of blocks are Fragmented (25-75% lines marked) and after each collection every block is in `unswept`, so by the next analysis they sit in `unswept`/`recycled`. Two defects:
(a) analyze_collection_strategy and candidate_block_bases only index head(0), overflow(1) and rest(2..); unswept/recycled blocks are never candidates.
(b) fragmentation >= 30% returns DefragmentationSweep, whose candidates() is empty ("TODO: all blocks"), so a heavily fragmented heap never evacuates at all.

Change (src/eval/memory/heap.rs only):
1. One HeapState helper enumerates bump blocks in a fixed order: head (0), overflow (1), then rest, unswept, recycled (2..). Analysis, stress mode and candidate_block_bases all use it, so indices agree; existing rest indices are unchanged. Line maps of unswept/recycled blocks are exactly the previous mark's, so their density estimate is sound. Evacuating from them needs nothing new: candidates are matched by base address, reset_region_marks/defer_sweep already cover both lists, and an evacuated block's lines stay unmarked so lazy sweep frees it and enforce_footprint_limit can release it.
2. Remove DefragmentationSweep; any fragmentation >= 10% yields SelectiveEvacuation.
3. Bound the copy: candidates (Sparse/Fragmented, unpinned) sorted by marked lines ascending, taken while their cumulative marked lines stay within a per-collection evacuation budget (sized by measurement; recorded in the PR), so cost per collection is bounded and the sparsest blocks (largest gain per copied line) go first.
4. Pinned blocks stay excluded; EU_GC_STRESS keeps forcing every unpinned block, now across all lists.

Verification: 228 at 12 MiB; Rust unit tests for (a) and (b), fault-injected; EU_GC_VERIFY=2, EU_GC_POISON=1, EU_GC_STRESS=1 harness; errors corpus in both prelude modes; benches 001-009, 015-022 interleaved A/B per PROTOCOL.
acceptance_criteria: Evacuation can select fragmented recycled or unswept blocks; 228 passes at a limit close to its live size; benches 001-009 and 015-022 not regressed (protocol); EU_GC_VERIFY=2 / POISON clean.
notes: PR #1185. Root cause: (a) candidates only from head/overflow/rest; (b) >=30% fragmentation gave DefragmentationSweep with no candidates, so heavy fragmentation never evacuated. (b) decides 228/test-compaction. Fix: candidates from every list; heavy fragmentation evacuates only when held > 3/4 limit (an evacuating GC updates all live objects); sparsest first within 1/8 of the heap's lines. test-compaction and 228 pass at 9-12 MiB (master fails at 12). Benches 0.94-1.03 (measured-single). Follow-up: evacuated blocks free only at the next GC (old copies stay line-marked), so EU_GC_STRESS holds ~2x live under tight limits. Report: docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-eu-oaz72.90-evacuate-fragmented-blocks.md
close_reason: Merged in PR #1185 (428b1f0). Two independent rig-reviews x2 rounds. Follow-ups reported to the coordinator.

title: (BUG) vec.nth silently maps a negative index to 0 instead of raising an error
description: Found by the external lane. [10, 20] vec.of vec.nth(-1) returns 10. A negative index should be an error naming the function and the index, consistent with list nth (eu-oaz72.43) and the non-integer decision (eu-oaz72.58). Check the other vec index intrinsics for the same clamp.
design:
Fix in the intrinsics (src/eval/stg/vec.rs, array.rs); no prelude change.
A shared helper in vec.rs converts an index argument: a non-number keeps its existing error; a non-integral number errors '<fn> <what> <n> must be an integer' (wording of eu-oaz72.58); a negative one errors '<fn> <what> <n> out of range: vec indices start at 0' (wording of list nth, eu-oaz72.43). Integral floats (2.0) are accepted.
- vec.nth: both checks; out-of-range message normalised to 'vec.nth index 5 out of range for vec of length 2' (list nth's form). Errors carry machine.annotation() instead of Smid::default().
- vec.slice: from/to get the same negative and non-integer checks; clamping of to past the end stays (documented), from > to stays empty.
- ndarray: negative coordinates already error (ArrayNegativeIndex). Non-integer coordinates/dimensions truncate silently (arr.get([0, 0.5]) reads [0,0]); num_list_to_usize_vec gains a non-integer error (new ArrayNonIntegerIndex variant). ARRAY.SLICE axis/index clamp negative to 0 and truncate non-integers: they go through the same checks.
- vec.sample/shuffle take random floats, not indices: unchanged.
Tests: checks in the existing vec harness file; one error fixture per function and case kind; fault-injection verified.
acceptance_criteria: vec.nth (and sibling vec index functions) with a negative or out-of-range index raise an error naming function and value; error fixture plus harness check, fault-injection verified.
